data.name: BIIRD
data.body: Dublin collective BIIRD are bringing a fresh energy to Irish traditional music, combining deep respect for the genre with a contemporary spirit and dynamic live presence. Their vibrant performances celebrate the richness of Irish musical traditions while introducing them to new audiences.

data.name: Sally C
data.body:
Whether via her DJ sets or label Big Saldo’s Chunkers, Sally C has developed one of the most distinctive sonic signatures in electronic music. The Belfast-born, Berlin-based artist traverses the gamut of vintage house, hip house, acid and breakbeat, all with that unmistakable Chunker sound.

Sally’s DJing journey begun in 2010 at the Reading Rooms in Dundee, Scotland, an iconic local club, playing host to the likes of DJ Pierre, DJ Sneak and Green Velvet. It was here she met an open-minded and accepting community and gained a crucial education in digging, mixing and all things dance music culture, an experience that would set her up for the rest of her career.

data.name: Muireann Bradley
data.body: Muireann Bradley is an 18-year-old Irish blues and folk guitarist and singer from Ballybofey, County Donegal. She specializes in fingerpicking styles of country blues and ragtime from the 1920s-40s, as well as later folk and Americana. Her debut album, "I Kept These Old Blues," was released in December 2023 and re-released by Decca Records/Verve Forecast in February 2025. She gained significant recognition after appearing on Jools' Annual Hootenanny on December 31, 2023.

data.name: Gurriers
data.body: Dublin’s Gurriers are one of Ireland’s most exciting new bands, delivering explosive post-punk packed with urgency, energy and razor-sharp social commentary. Their intense live shows and powerful sound have quickly earned them a reputation as a must-see act on the rising Irish music scene.

data.name: Sexy Tadhg
data.body: A fearless force in Ireland’s alternative music landscape, SexyTadhg blends electrifying pop, punk attitude and theatrical performance into a celebration of self-expression. Bold, unapologetic and impossible to ignore, their live shows are a vibrant explosion of music, activism and queer joy.

data.name: Huartan (DJ Set)
data.body: Emerging from the Gaeltacht quarter of West Belfast, Huartan is formed by three Irish traditional musicians – Catriona Ní Ghribín, Múlú, and producer Stiofán Ó Luachráin – alongside masked performers embodying the síogaí (fairy folk). As Hot Press write, Huartan are “one of the key voices in a realignment of modern Irish music and culture”: rooted in decolonial and anti-capitalist ideals, their otherworldly live shows channel a mythic pre-Christian Ireland. In 2026, the band will be touring their self-titled debut album, featuring Gaeilge songs injected with “urgent, pulsating electronica” (Hot Press) and described by Chordblossom as “one of the most visionary albums from 2025”.

data.name: Shark School
data.body: Shark School is an Irish band formed in June 2023, known for their unique blend of garage rock and performance art, described as "somewhere between a basement show and a performance art piece". They are characterized by their sarcastic, energetic performances and a focus on delivering a spectacle, sometimes resulting in a "delightfully sideways" atmosphere, as noted by Roisin Dubh.

data.name: Zaska
data.body:
ZASKA plays neo-soul infused with indie jazz and a touch of funk. Max Zaska is an Irish guitarist, songwriter, musical director, and producer known for his collaborations with many Irish artists, including Hozier.

Max Zaska blends influences from Silk Sonic, Snarky Puppy, Tom Misch and Nubiyan Twist with a guitar style that pulls from greats Wes Montgomery, John Scofield, Nile Rodgers, and Carlos Santana to create a sound uniquely ZASKA.

data.name: Glasshouse presents: Bjork
data.body: A celebration of one of music's most visionary artists, Glasshouse Presents: Björk explores the groundbreaking catalogue of the Icelandic icon through a specially curated listening experience. Expect innovation, emotion and a deep dive into a truly singular musical world.

data.name: Nialler9
data.body: Niall Byrne, known as Nialler9, is an Irish music event curator, producer, and DJ, as well as the founder of the influential Irish music website Nialler9. He's also a music supervisor and consultant, known for his work in digital media, advertising, and film, with a focus on emerging Irish music.

data.name: Molly Donnery
data.body: Harpist and folk songwriter Molly Donnery is one the most quietly powerful voices in Irish music. Her music is gently introspective, tracing themes of longing, growth, and self-discovery.

data.name: Organ Freeman (Live Jazz)
data.body: Organ Freeman is a Dublin-based jazz organ trio featuring Charlie Moon (guitar/vocals), Darragh Hennessy (organ), and Dominic Mullan (drums). For the past seven years they’ve been the resident band at The Big Romance, where their weekly shows have become a cornerstone of the city’s jazz scene. Blending blues, bebop, funk, and standards—with regular guest musicians and jam sessions the band is known for high-energy, unpredictable live performances.

data.name: The Wran
data.body: Hailing from the Comeragh Mountains of County Waterford, The Wran are four brothers: Tommy, Danny, Seán and Stephen Dunford. They bring a fresh voice to Irish music, blending trad with punk and a hint of psychedelia to create music that feels both timeless and new. Drawing inspiration from Planxty, The Pogues and Lankum. The Wran combines traditional and modern instrumentation, including banjo, harmonium, acoustic guitar, bass VI and drums. They are dedicated to keeping the Irish language, traditional songs and storytelling alive while continuing to push it forward in their own way.

data.name: Sing Along Social
data.body: The Sing Along Social specialise in singing parties designed for people who can't sing. Hosted by The Craic Mechanics, they have been popping up at parties, festivals and residencies in Ireland, the UK and beyond since 2015. They create a safe and gas space where friends and strangers gather together to sing along to their favourite cheesy pop songs. Sort of like group karaoke but with no microphones and with nobody being put on the spot. You don't have to practice, you don't need to know the words and you don't even need to be able to sing.

data.name: Trinity Orchestra
data.body: Known for reimagining modern classics through the power of a full orchestra, Trinity Orchestra brings a fresh perspective to contemporary music. Made up of talented student musicians, the ensemble has become renowned for its ambitious performances that bridge the worlds of classical and popular music.

data.name: Kean Kavanagh
data.body: Texas born, Portlaoise raised singer, songwriter, producer and co-founder of Soft Boy Records, Kean Kavanagh has become one of Ireland's most distinctive musical voices. His acclaimed debut album, The County Star, was hailed as "a beautiful yet haunting masterpiece", weaving together vivid storytelling, folklore-inspired lyricism and characters shaped by his Texan roots and Laois upbringing. Blending Americana, indie, showband rock'n'roll and Irish traditional psychedelia, Kean creates a sound that is uniquely his own.

data.name: Avenue 68
data.body: Dublin-based band of 5-best friends who share a love for all things music, Avenue 68,  are the freshest faces of RnB/Soul, Jazz. Taking influence from artists like Eryka Badu, D’Angelo and Olivia Dean, this band explores sexuality, relationships and identity through silky smooth vocals, intricate guitar lines and melodies. This groovy 5-piece is not one to be missed.

data.name: Cáit
data.body: Cáit is a Dublin‑born DJ and photographer, a key resident at Berlin‑based Radiant Love and Dublin’s intimate party series Dip.Playing since around 2014, she’s brought her dreamy, cosmic house and trance‑inflected sets to venues like District 8 (Dublin), Renate (Berlin), and S13 Warehouse (Belfast). Cáit blends immersive music with vibrant visuals, channeling a colorful, community-first creative ethos.

data.name: Rhyzine
data.body: Rhyzine is a tour de force of the dance, emerging as one of Dublin’s most exciting clubbing voices as a DJ and co-founder of the celebrated party HONEYPOT. In such a remarkably short space of time, Rhyzine has left an indelible mark on their local scene. Their pro-community approach to nightlife, providing marginalised queer voices with a space to dance and DJ, has helped foster one of the best parties and collectives in the country. Their exhilarating genre-less approach to sets allow selections to focus on energy and drama, lending dance floors with the right tools to liberate their bodies within the dance. It’s a palpable feeling you can sense throughout every set they do, a deft kinetic momentum offset by angular basslines and rave-ready melodics.

data.name: Surusinghe
data.body: Surusinghe is a Melbourne-born, London-based DJ and producer known for genre-defying sets that fuse bass, reggaeton, techno, and broken rhythms.

data.name: Dylan Fogarty
data.body:
Dublin-based techno artist Dylan Fogarty has been at the forefront of his city’s techno revival.

Embracing the playful, loop-driven approach of ‘00s techno while weaving in elements of house, garage, and dub. His sound, a rich tapestry of groove, swing, and unadulterated funk, channels the golden era of techno, striking a balance between Stockholm and Napoli while shaping the next generation of the genre in Ireland and beyond.

data.name: Collie
data.body: Collie (Colm McKenna) is a Dublin-based selector, known for digging deep into vinyl, digital and self-produced cuts to craft atmospheric, skin-tingling sets.

data.name: Tony Cantwell
data.body: Tony Cantwell is one of Ireland’s most original and unpredictable comedy talents. Known for his viral sketches, podcast Tony Cantwell’s Hit Show, and totally unfiltered stand-up, he’s built a cult following with his surreal characters and offbeat charm. A natural on stage, Tony’s live shows are riotous, high-energy trips into the bizarre corners of his brain. Whether he’s riffing on childhood nostalgia or delivering absurd observations, you’re guaranteed a belly laugh. Don’t miss him.

data.name: Prymary Colours
data.body:
Have you ever seen bubbles sparkling on a red hot bassline? PrYmary Colours are that sparkle- and are heating up stages all over the world. There's music & there's dance. There's performance & there's aesthetics. And there's PrYmary Colours, who fuse them all together in one neat pumping package!

Having played at the House Of Yes club in New York, and the Olympia in Dublin, along with a host of festivals such as Electric Picnic, Beyond The Pale, Life and Forbidden Fruit, MOTHER Pride and All Together Now, and most recently Latitude UK, there's no stage these guys can't fill. 

PrYmary Colours offer, a duo performance in DJ & Singer for club events or the full live show experience for festival stages, with dancers, hula hoopers, costumes, confetti, bubbles, visuals, cold sparkles, lights and more.

data.name: Playback Presents: Stop Making Sense
data.body: Playback is an "album tribute" band. Covering classic rock albums from start to finish, rounding out our sets with greatest hits.

data.name: New Jackson
data.body: New Jackson is the electronic alias of Dublin producer, singer, and DJ David Kitt. Fusing warm analog synths, deep house grooves, and textured vocals, his music is immersive, melodic, and emotionally rich.

data.name: Meg Reilly
data.body: Fewcans (Meg Reilly) is a Dublin comic known for her sharp, self-deprecating humour and spot-on sketches about Irish life. From chaotic nights out to awkward small talk, her viral videos capture the cringe and charm of everyday moments with hilarious honesty. Now bringing her online wit to the live stage.

data.name: Ryan Carrick
data.body: Dublin-born comedian, content creator and stand‑up rising star, Ryan Carrick rings energetic observational stand‑up to the stage, infused with playful Dublin charm.

data.name: The Wild Geeze - Comedy Cabaret
data.body: The Wild Geeze are an Irish female comedic duo bringing queer cabaret to ATN23, fromed by Breda Larkin from the dykes of Ballinasloe, and burlesque chanteuse and body-positive activist Miss Lavelle from Limerick city. A wild and hilarious display of raw female-led comedy with hand-picked guest acts, including some token males. Born performers, we go hard, leaving our souls, hearts, and moon cups on the stage. If you like body positivity, saving the trees, and songs about Gees then our shows are for you.

data.name: Aoife Dunne
data.body: Aoife Dunne has become one of Ireland’s fastest-rising comedians since making her stand-up debut in November 2023. Her smash-hit debut show, Good Grief, has sold out theatres across Ireland and earned critical acclaim at the Edinburgh Fringe. Blending razor-sharp observations with quick-fire crowd work and infectious energy, Aoife has quickly become one of the most exciting new names on the Irish comedy circuit.

data.name: Peter McGann
data.body: Peter McGann is an Irish comedian, actor, writer and director from Rathdrum, County Wicklow, now based in Sandymount, Dublin. He holds a Master’s in screenwriting from the University of Galway, and first rose to prominence with viral comedy sketches during the 2020 COVID‑19 lockdown. Since then he's released a stand‑up tour (“Great Lad,” 2024), written/directed short films, and contributed to projects like the Bureau de Change Song Contest

data.name: Martin Angolo
data.body: Martin Angolo is an award-winning Irish comedian known for sharp wit and standout storytelling. He's performed worldwide and appeared on LOL: Last One Laughing Ireland.

data.name: Róis
data.body: Róis (Rose Connolly) is a composer, multi‑instrumentalist, and singer from County Fermanagh, with dynamic live shows that reinterpret the Irish wake as both cathartic and celebratory, Róis transports audiences into a brave new realm of sonic ritual and emotional release

data.name: Kate Brennan Harding
data.body: Kate Brennan Harding is a Galway-born DJ, broadcaster, and music curator known for her genre-spanning, feel-good sets blending house, disco, techno, and electro. A passionate advocate for Irish artists, she brings deep cuts, uplifting grooves, and inclusive energy to every dancefloor.

data.name: Selky
data.body: After turning Cambium Club on its head at ATN '25, Selky is back for a victory lap! His genre-hopping sets weave together surgical vogue cuts, breakbeats, club rollers, and unexpected pop moments with a knack for pressure switches and peak-time payoffs. Whether it's a sweaty club or a sun-soaked field, the Club Comfort don delivers big energy, bigger blends, and the kind of dancefloor momentum that keeps crowds bumpin'.

And He, The Fool
data.body: Dublin-based septet blending art rock, psychedelic pop, and neo-soul. Formed in 2022, their sound weaves theatricality with emotional depth, moving from melancholic introspection to celebratory grooves.

data.name: David Kitt
data.body: Irish singer-songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist, David Kitt, crosses multiple genres. His music is unusual, yet immediately likeable and the signature genre-blending is imaginative, effective and never, ever predictable.

data.name: Negro Impacto
data.body:
Negro Impacto are the independent Irish duo who have been quietly
setting the standard for alternative RnB and against-the-grain artistry in
the Irish music scene. The Dundalk band comprises of Chi-chi and
StrangeLove who together have created a fresh, indie, soulful sound which along with their incredible live show, has landed them on prestigious one-to-watch lists, multiple Spotify editorial covers and cemented their position as a staple on the Irish festival and event circuit year round. Negro Impacto have captivated audiences far and wide, from Primavera Pro Barcelona and Mladi Ladi Jazz Festival Prague to Ireland Music Week,
performing for the President of Ireland, selected for RTÉ 2FM Rising and opening for icons like Madness, Ojerime and STRFKR.

data.name: Elikya
data.body: Based in Ireland, Elikya has spent over 20 years as ambassadors of Congolese music. This 9-piece band blends rumba, dance, and bass-driven grooves with sweet Lingala vocals, hypnotic guitars, and relentless percussion. Known for their precision, full-band choreography, and vibrant style, Elikya channels the rich tradition of Congolese music into unforgettable, high-energy performances.

data.name: Dónal Dineen with Hewan Mulugeta and Special Guests
megaTRAD
data.body: megaTRAD are a high energy, improvisation based trio with a sound best described as an exalted manifestation of Irish Trad, melding their cultural musical heritage with diverse individual musical experiences, bolstered by the contemporary nuances of stomp, bass, and pedal FX boards. The outcome is an innovative and exhilarating auditory journey, affectionately termed "Tradscendental" by their enthusiastic fanbase. Their improvisational approach to the megaTRAD show promises audiences a once-in-a-lifetime experience at every performance and gives megaTRAD the freedom to sculpt their performance around what energy the audience is looking for.

data.name: Trad Folkin Raps - Strange Boy, Dyrt, Hazey Haze
Earthman Bob's Guide to Raving
data.body: Join Earthman Bob on his quest to reimagine the future of humanity and the Earth through poetry, music and dance. Together with Earthman Bob and his cosmic crew we’ll learn how to dance our way through the existential questions of climate catastrophe and the meta-crisis and towards a Utopian space station in the sky. Join him for spoken word, music, poetry, and dance workshops as we map out a path for our species' away from the precipice of catastrophe and toward a world worth fighting for.

data.name: Acid Granny Presents Schindler's Fist
data.body: Acid Granny presents Düblin’s dürtiest germans: SCHINDLER’S FIST. Witness the pure mechanical power of a full live band, pumping endless improvised techno out of every orifice. Bring your best leather or worst bin bag and get fisted!

Grooveline
data.body: Grooveline is a bilingual, high-octane sextet from the northwest of Ireland, blending funk, hip-hop, rock, jazz, and trad into a fresh, genre-bending sound. Described by HotPress as “Vulfpeck’s precision, Parliament’s cool, and James Brown’s energy,” they’re fronting a new wave of Irish-language music. Known for explosive live shows, catchy raps, and wild energy, Grooveline delivers a rhythm-driven experience that gets crowds moving and keeps the craic alive.

Patrick De Vallette
data.body:
Patrick de Valette is a French actor, comedian, and clown known for his iconoclastic style and bold stage presence. A founding member of the cult comedy troupe Les Chiche Capon since 2001, he also performed with Cirque du Soleil in Banana Shpeel in New York in 2010. Since 2014, he has toured his acclaimed solo show Hobobo, appearing in Paris and regularly at the Avignon Festival. On screen, he stars in the film Fêlés alongside Pierre Richard and Les Chiche Capon, and features in Yórgos Lánthimos’s Poor Things. He also appears in the Apple TV+ series À l’ombre des forêts with Benoît Magimel and in the upcoming Lucky Luke series for Disney+.
Under the name DJ Patrick Swayze, he spins wildly eclectic sets — from old-school hip-hop to 1950s Japanese ballads… and everything in between. There’s funk, there’s weird stuff, and there’s a whole lot of love. The goal? To dance, baby.

data.name: Tonie Walsh
data.body: "The Sleazemaster" for his unrivaled selection of duurty disco, funk and deep house, Tonie Walsh has been a totemic presence on the Irish club scene since 1979. Ping Pong Disco at ATN, an annual pilgrimage according to Tonie, is one of his increasingly rare dj appearances.

data.name: Sonic Sermon with Odhrán
data.body: Odhrán is a DJ from Dublin specialising in Disco, Italo, and all funky cosmic things in between. Expect an anything goes approach to mixing with a playful selection of deep disko cuts throughout.

Dry Cleaning
data.body: South London post-punk outfit Dry Cleaning have carved out a distinctive sound built around angular guitars, hypnotic rhythms and the deadpan delivery of vocalist Florence Shaw. Sharp, unconventional and endlessly compelling, the band has become one of the most celebrated names in contemporary alternative music.

data.name: Sloucho
data.body: Sloucho is an Irish producer and audiovisual artist known for blending bass-heavy beats with immersive visuals. His genre-defying sound explores themes of identity and digital life, with standout releases like his debut album NPC and the conceptual ECHOES EP. Sloucho’s live shows create a unique, mind-bending sensory experience that pushes the boundaries of electronic music.

data.name: Alba b2b K8olo (2muchbootyinthebooth)
data.body:
K8olo and Alba, better known as 2muchbootyinthebooth, whose joyful approach to club music perfectly captures a festival's ethos.
Reggaeton, Baltimore club , ragga, Riko Dan edits and Latin percussion collide in a set that refuses to recognise genre boundaries. Playful without ever becoming ironic, their selections balance deep knowledge with flirty, infectious fun.

data.name: BLKCNVS
data.body: Blkcnvs is a Dublin-based African-Irish DJ who has been collecting and mixing his musical tastes over the years. He uses his worldly palate to create space for letting loose, rediscovering play, and dancing. As the founder of The Sweet Spot, he focuses on creating a comfortable social space to celebrate music and dance, fostering warm connections where differences can be celebrated—from Ireland to the world.

data.name: DJ Shaz
data.body: DJ Shaz is a genre-bending DJ bringing together house, Afro house, techno, and club sounds. Known for high energy sets, uplifting dance floor experiences, and a commitment to empowering women in music through HerSet. Creating moments, building community, and keeping the crowd moving.

data.name: Ciara May
data.body:
Ciara May is a west coast deejay who always brings a diverse plethora of genres.
Returning to Cambium Club, for this set, expect anything from Cumbia to Desi,
SWANA to Balkan, soca to Funkhall. Whether from behind the decks or running Cultúr/Riot, Galway’s inclusive Queer Club Night, she cultivates a sound to facilitate connection on the dancefloor; to each other, to our bodies and where people are free to be, feel safe, have fun and be a bit silly.

Donal Dineen’s Backstory with B+, Hewan Mulugeta & Guests
data.body:
Dónal Dineen’s Backstory Dances have gone from strength to strength recently with
a storied residency at the Commercial Rowing Club in Dublin continuing to hold
down an exalted posi=on within the capital’s underground dance scene.
He has brought all the Backstory energy to bear on the Cambium stage at All together Now
in 2023 & 2024 and he returns this year with wind in his sails from acclaimed runs on the
radio shows Mystery Train, Blue of the Night and Vesperine on RTE Lyric FM.
Dónal’s extended Backstory sets are like alterna=ve guides to the musical universe
with no stone leP unturned in his mission to unearth gems from every musical
hotspot the world over.
The impetus to start the night back in 2015 stemmed from his desire to find a home
for the kind of dance music fire that he was unearthing in his search for tunes in
dusty basements of record stores worldwide to write about for his Sunken Treasure
column in the Irish Times.
It began as a project to gather together all the sounds he was collecting on vinyl from
every part of the world and became a place for the like-minded to revel in the joy of music and the uniquely special experience of discovering it together on a dance- floor. The unerring attention to detail on the quality of the music has seen its reputation soar to become something of a touchstone for discerning dancers both in
Dublin town and further afield.
The Backstory motto “All the colours, every dancing mood” has served it well and the
atmosphere generated on one heady night aPer another has become the stuff of
legend from its genesis in its spiritual home of the much-missed Jigsaw in the north
inner city to its current incarna=on by the Liffey Banks.

data.name: DJ Egg
data.body: DJ Egg is a music selector and artist who has been steadily rising and creating communities on the dance floor through the Irish and UK scenes for the past seven years. Well-established in the jungle and bass scene, they have married their passion for bass-heavy music with their long-standing involvement in grassroots queer culture, developing a signature sound that encompasses euphoric queer house and club music into their sets. They are a resident of Dublin Digital Radio and co-run Dyke Nite (Limerick) and are the resident designer and frequent performer of Ar Ais Arís.

data.name: BIG CHEEKS
data.body: BIG CHEEKS is a Rwandan DJ based in Dublin, Ireland; who brings an infectious energy to any event with groovy and body shaking selections from Afrobeats, to R&B, Soul, Hip-Hop, Dancehall, Balie Funk, Amapiano and much more.

data.name: Mynameisjohn
data.body: Mynameisjohn is John Lillis, an artist, DJ and record collector living in Liscannor, Co. Clare. John has over 20 years experience DJing around the country and abroad. An avid and all-round music fan, John's taste is rooted in the exotic and unfamiliar, but always with an eye on the dance floor. He knows his way around a turntable and mixer, ranging from the relaxed to the ruckus, and you can expect to hear Cormac Begley beside Marcus Valle, and Brìghde Chaimbeul mixed into Moodymann. John runs the event series Idir Dhá Thrá in Co. Clare and is part of the Sunday Spinners DJ collective. Up the banner!

data.name: Jacqui Kelleher
data.body: Whether dropping an Afrobeat gem into a set of Latin boogaloo or seamlessly bridging SWANA grooves with American soul, Jacqui loves nothing more than a dance at the cultural crossroads filled with musical handbrake turns.

data.name: B+
data.body: Brian “B+” Cross is a photographer and filmmaker known for iconic album covers and music films. He’s worked with artists like J Dilla, Eazy-E, Madlib, Thundercat, and Kamasi Washington, and was director of photography for Exit Through the Gift Shop. Co-founder of Mochilla and former photo editor of Wax Poetics, B+ is also the author of It’s Not About a Salary and Ghostnotes. He lives in LA, teaches at UC San Diego, and is currently completing a film on The Supremes' 1981 Ireland tour.

data.name: Hewan Mulugeta
data.body: Hewan is one of Backstory's key DJs in residence. Born and raised in Ethiopia, she brings an immense amount of knowledge to each and every one of her singular sets. Playing mainly grooves from the 1960s and 70s golden era of modern Ethiopian music, she also incorporates a range of other African sounds into a glorious melting pot that never fails to set the night on fire.

data.name: Paídí Cronin
data.body: As both promoter and DJ, Paídí Cronin has been instrumental in keeping the town of Tralee and Kerry in general safe for great music, decades hence. Returning to the Cambium for the first time since his storming set in 2023, Paídí will be conjuring a journey into sound like no other from a record collection that spans dance floor jazz, rhythm&blues, explosive early rock'n'roll and every colour and shade of electronic music.

Ispíní na hÉireann host the Citizen Ceili
data.body:
Ispíní na hÉireann are a feral Folk-Alternative Irish music collective from Dublin, Ireland.

They formed in 2018 and are fronted by Tomás Mulligan, Paahto Cummins, and Declan Gillen. Steeped in Dublin's rich traditional music scene, the band brings together some of Ireland's most exciting and talented contemporary musicians, cultivating a sound that is fiercely original and unmistakably Irish. Their music blends virtuosic original compositions with bold re-imaginings of classic tunes, fusing technical mastery with sharp wit, storytelling, and social commentary — creating performances that are as thought-provoking as they are electrifying.

Following the success of their debut album The Hard Working Men, the band released their critically acclaimed second record Poxtail Soup, showcasing their trademark mix of energy, irreverence, and heart. With a growing audience across Ireland, the UK, and Europe, and a reputation for exhilarating live shows, Ispíní na hÉireann continue to redefine what contemporary Irish music can be.

data.name: Calum Agnew
data.body: Composing and directing a full 8-piece band in his signature thrifted pinstripe suit, Calum brings an unapologetic mod-meets-modern energy to both his music and his live shows. There’s a mischievous charm to it all, theatrical, a bit glam, but rooted in raw, soulful vulnerability. With a seductive vocal tone and a knack for weaving intricately catchy pop melodies through soulful, jazz-leaning arrangements, Calum lands somewhere between Amy Winehouse, Joy Crookes, and RAYE but with a vision and direction unmistakably his own, and unlike anything else in Ireland right now.

data.name: Sahana
data.body: Sahana is a Dublin-based DJ known for weaving together house, techno, tribal rhythms and SWANA-inspired sounds into captivating, genre-spanning sets. A resident with Klub Sukar and The Midnight Disco, she brings infectious energy, global influences and a fearless approach to every dancefloor.

Pulp
data.body: Britpop icons Pulp return with their signature blend of sharp storytelling, wit and irresistible indie anthems. Fronted by the charismatic Jarvis Cocker, the Sheffield legends remain one of the UK’s most influential bands, with classics like Common People, Disco 2000 and Do You Remember the First Time? continuing to fill dancefloors decades later.

data.name: KNEECAP
data.body: Belfast rap trio KNEECAP have become one of the most talked-about acts in contemporary music, fusing Irish-language hip-hop with sharp humour, political commentary and explosive energy. Their boundary-pushing sound and unforgettable live performances have earned them a devoted following far beyond Ireland.

data.name: The Mary Wallopers
data.body: Blending traditional Irish folk with sharp wit, rebellious spirit and boundless energy, The Mary Wallopers have become one of Ireland’s most beloved live acts. Known for breathing new life into centuries-old songs while tackling modern themes, their performances are equal parts celebration, storytelling and singalong.

data.name: Ezra Collective
data.body: Mercury Prize-winning quintet Ezra Collective fuse jazz, afrobeat, hip-hop, reggae and soul into a sound that is uniquely their own. Renowned for their joyous, high-energy live shows, the London group has become one of the leading voices in a new generation of British jazz.

data.name: Disclosure (DJ)
data.body: One half of the Grammy-nominated duo Disclosure, Guy Lawrence brings the group’s signature blend of house, garage and electronic music to the decks for an unforgettable DJ set. Expect dancefloor-ready anthems, infectious grooves and a masterclass in modern electronic music from one of the genre’s most influential names.

data.name: Underworld
data.body: Electronic pioneers Underworld have spent decades pushing the boundaries of dance music with their hypnotic blend of techno, house and experimental sounds. Known for iconic tracks such as Born Slippy (Nuxx) and their immersive live performances, the duo remain one of the most influential acts in electronic music.

data.name: Christy Moore
data.body: One of Ireland’s most revered and influential musicians, Christy Moore has spent decades shaping the landscape of Irish folk music. Renowned for his powerful voice, masterful storytelling and timeless songs, his performances continue to resonate with audiences across generations.

data.name: Maribou State (Live)
data.body: Combining organic instrumentation with lush electronic production, Maribou State have become one of the most beloved acts in modern electronic music. Their warm, melodic sound blends elements of house, ambient and downtempo music, creating immersive live experiences that are both euphoric and deeply emotive.

data.name: Self Esteem
data.body: The musical project of Rebecca Lucy Taylor, Self Esteem has earned widespread acclaim for her bold, empowering pop that blends sharp lyricism with infectious hooks. Honest, fearless and deeply personal, her music tackles everything from relationships to self-worth, making her one of the UK's most compelling contemporary artists.

data.name: Floating Points (Live)
data.body: Producer, composer and multi-instrumentalist Floating Points is renowned for seamlessly blending electronic music, jazz and classical influences into expansive sonic journeys. His live performances showcase intricate musicianship and innovative sound design, creating immersive experiences that blur the lines between club culture and contemporary composition.

data.name: Mall Grab
data.body: Mall Grab has become one of the defining names of modern electronic music, known for his raw, high-energy blend of house, techno and rave influences. Whether producing anthems or commanding festival stages, he brings intensity, emotion and undeniable energy to every performance.

data.name: Mogwai
data.body: Scottish post-rock pioneers Mogwai have spent nearly three decades crafting expansive, atmospheric soundscapes that move effortlessly between delicate beauty and thunderous intensity. Renowned for their cinematic compositions and powerful live performances, they remain one of the most influential instrumental bands of their generation.

data.name: Damien Dempsey
data.body: A treasured voice in Irish music, Damien Dempsey combines folk, traditional Irish influences and socially conscious songwriting to powerful effect. Known for his heartfelt lyrics and passionate performances, he has built a devoted following through songs that celebrate community, resilience and identity.

data.name: Kae Tempest
data.body: A celebrated poet, playwright and recording artist, Kae Tempest is renowned for their powerful storytelling and thought-provoking lyricism. Blending spoken word, hip-hop and contemporary music, their work explores identity, connection and the human experience with remarkable honesty and intensity.

data.name: Annie Mac
data.body: Annie Macmanus is an author, broadcaster and DJ. Over her 20 year career in the arts, she has created a far reaching cultural presence, rooted in quality, integrity, and authenticity. Annie has a strong legacy of seventeen years presenting flagship music shows on BBC Radio 1. She has been a key music industry figure championing female and LGBTQ+ artists and advocating for positive, inclusive change.

data.name: Chet Faker
data.body: Australian artist Chet Faker blends soulful vocals, electronic production and introspective songwriting into a sound that is instantly recognisable. Rising to international acclaim with his distinctive take on electronic soul, he continues to captivate audiences with his genre-crossing music and magnetic live performances.

data.name: Kerri Chandler
data.body: A true house music icon, Kerri Chandler has spent decades shaping the sound of dance music with his soulful grooves, impeccable production and masterful DJ sets. Revered by generations of artists and clubbers alike, he remains one of the most influential figures in house music history.

data.name: The Avalanches (DJ Set)
data.body: Australian electronic legends The Avalanches are renowned for their genre-defying sound, weaving together samples, beats and musical influences from across the globe. Their DJ sets are eclectic, uplifting and packed with surprises, taking audiences on a journey through dance music, disco, hip-hop and beyond.

data.name: Gilla Band
data.body: One of Ireland’s most boundary-pushing bands, Gilla Band are renowned for their intense blend of noise rock, post-punk and experimental music. Their uncompromising sound, relentless energy and thrilling live shows have established them as a standout force in contemporary alternative music.

data.name: Barrington Levy
data.body: A true reggae icon, Barrington Levy has been one of Jamaica’s most influential voices for over four decades. Known for his distinctive vocal style and timeless hits, he has helped shape the sound of dancehall and reggae, inspiring generations of artists across the globe.

data.name: Jyoty
data.body: Amsterdam-born DJ and broadcaster Jyoty has become one of the most exciting selectors in contemporary music. Renowned for her genre-spanning sets, she effortlessly blends hip-hop, soul, house, amapiano and global sounds, creating vibrant dancefloor experiences that celebrate musical discovery.

data.name: Greentea Peng
data.body: Blending neo-soul, reggae, psychedelic influences and alternative R&B, Greentea Peng has carved out a unique space in contemporary music. Known for her soulful vocals, introspective songwriting and genre-defying sound, she delivers performances that are both captivating and deeply immersive.

data.name: For Those I Love
data.body:
David Balfe, the songwriter, producer and visual creative behind Dublin’s For Those I Love has become one of Ireland’s most acclaimed contemporary voices, merging local storytelling with electronic music to explore class, grief, modern life and the friendships that underpin it.
His self-titled 2021 debut earned widespread critical praise along with the Choice Music Prize, as his follow up Carving The Stone turned its gaze more critically inward, with a darker twist. His live shows combine a love for intimate performance with the theatrical, bringing together the spoken word and rattling club numbers.

data.name: Soda Blonde
data.body: Dublin four-piece Soda Blonde craft atmospheric indie-pop filled with rich melodies, emotional depth and cinematic production. Led by the captivating vocals of Faye O’Rourke, the band have established themselves as one of Ireland’s most exciting contemporary acts through their introspective songwriting and captivating live shows.

data.name: Kate Nash
data.body: Singer, songwriter and actress Kate Nash became a defining voice of British indie-pop with her witty lyricism, distinctive style and candid storytelling. From chart-topping hits to fiercely independent releases, she has continued to evolve as an artist while remaining unapologetically authentic and influential.

data.name: Sprints
data.body: Dublin post-punk quartet Sprints have quickly emerged as one of Ireland’s most exciting guitar bands. Driven by fierce energy, sharp songwriting and commanding live performances, the band’s sound combines punk urgency with raw emotion and fearless intensity.

data.name: Anna von Hausswolff
data.body: Swedish composer, singer and multi-instrumentalist Anna von Hausswolff is celebrated for her powerful voice and expansive, genre-defying sound. Blending elements of folk, drone, gothic rock and experimental music, she creates deeply atmospheric performances that are both haunting and profoundly moving.

data.name: Joy Orbison
data.body: One of the most influential producers and DJs of the past decade, Joy Orbison has continually reshaped the sound of UK electronic music. Blending house, garage, bass and techno with effortless style, his sets are both deeply musical and relentlessly danceable.

data.name: Job Jobse
data.body: Few DJs command a dancefloor quite like Job Jobse. The Amsterdam favourite has earned a cult following through marathon sets that effortlessly move between house, techno, disco and euphoric rave moments. Expect a journey packed with surprises, emotion and unforgettable energy.

data.name: The Dare (DJ Set)
data.body: The Dare has emerged as one of the most talked-about names in contemporary dance and indie club culture, combining sharp electronic production with a rebellious, party-starting energy. Expect a high-intensity DJ set packed with infectious beats, underground influences and late-night dancefloor anthems.

data.name: Swimming Paul
data.body: Swimming Paul creates immersive electronic music that drifts effortlessly between ambient textures, downtempo grooves and euphoric club influences. Blending lush production with emotive melodies and cinematic soundscapes, his performances offer a captivating journey that is equally suited to deep listening and the dancefloor.

data.name: Weval (Live)
data.body: Dutch duo Weval are renowned for their rich blend of electronic music, live instrumentation and immersive sound design. Combining intricate production with emotive melodies and hypnotic rhythms, their live performances create a captivating journey that moves seamlessly between the dancefloor and deep listening.

data.name: Sam Alfred
data.body: Melbourne's Sam Alfred has rapidly emerged as one of Australia's most exciting electronic artists. Blending uplifting house, melodic grooves and infectious energy, his sets strike the perfect balance between deep musicality and hands-in-the-air moments.

data.name: KhakiKid
data.body: One of Ireland’s most exciting emerging artists, KhakiKid blends hip-hop, indie, electronic and alternative influences into a sound that is fresh, unpredictable and distinctly his own. His sharp lyricism, creative production and energetic performances have quickly earned him a growing fanbase.

data.name: Say She She
data.body: Brooklyn trio Say She She channel the spirit of classic disco, funk and soul while bringing a modern perspective to their music. With lush harmonies, infectious grooves and empowering messages, they have quickly earned a reputation for delivering uplifting and irresistible live performances.

data.name: Getdown Services
data.body: Bristol duo Getdown Services have built a cult following with their offbeat blend of dance-punk, electro, indie and razor-sharp social commentary. Equal parts absurd, hilarious and unexpectedly heartfelt, their songs turn everyday British life into infectious, tongue-in-cheek anthems. Known for their chaotic, high-energy live shows, Getdown Services are guaranteed to deliver one of the weekend's most entertaining sets.

data.name: Jacob Alon
data.body: Scottish singer-songwriter Jacob Alon is one of the most compelling new voices in contemporary folk. Blending delicate fingerpicked guitar with an ethereal, emotionally rich vocal, their music draws on traditional folk, indie and intimate storytelling to create songs of remarkable depth and vulnerability. With a rapidly growing reputation for captivating live performances, Jacob Alon is an artist destined to leave a lasting impression.

data.name: Brògeal
data.body: Hailing from Falkirk, Brògeal are breathing new life into Celtic folk with a raucous mix of traditional influences, indie swagger and punk spirit. Their foot-stomping anthems, singalong choruses and infectious storytelling have earned them a reputation as one of the UK's most exciting live acts. Equal parts ceilidh and chaos, Brògeal bring the kind of high-energy performance that turns every crowd into a party.

data.name: Moonchild Sanelly
data.body: South African artist Moonchild Sanelly is a trailblazing performer known for her bold fusion of electronic music, hip-hop, afro-pop and dance. With her vibrant stage presence, fearless creativity and infectious energy, she has become one of the most distinctive and exciting voices in contemporary African music.

data.name: Rose Betts
data.body: Singer-songwriter Rose Betts crafts heartfelt indie-pop infused with cinematic melodies and emotionally resonant storytelling. With a voice that effortlessly balances vulnerability and strength, she has built a growing international audience through songs that explore love, self-discovery and human connection.

data.name: Cardinals
data.body: Cork five-piece Cardinals are quickly making their mark with a stirring blend of indie rock, post-punk and Irish folk influences. Balancing soaring melodies with raw emotion and cinematic intensity, the band have earned a reputation as one of Ireland's most exciting new acts. With anthemic songs and captivating live performances, Cardinals are a band destined for much bigger stages.

data.name: O'Flynn
data.body: O’Flynn is a London DJ and producer known for feel-good, rhythm-driven sets that sit somewhere between underground club heat and full festival release. Blending house, UK bass and global club sounds, he’s built a reputation for turning dancefloors into pure energy. Expect rolling grooves, surprise drops and a set that keeps the field moving from start to finish.

data.name: David Keenan
data.body: David Keenan is an Irish singer-songwriter known for his poetic lyricism, raw storytelling and deeply emotive live performances. Hailing from Dundalk, his songs move between intimate folk and sweeping, spoken-word intensity, capturing everyday life with vivid honesty and heart. A powerful presence on stage, Keenan delivers sets that feel both personal and transcendent.

data.name: King Kong Company
data.body: Known for their high-octane live shows, King Kong Company fuse electronic beats, live instrumentation and infectious energy into a genre-defying party experience. The Waterford outfit have built a loyal following through their explosive performances, turning every stage into a celebration.

data.name: Hot 8 Brass Band
data.body: Hailing from New Orleans, Hot 8 Brass Band blend traditional brass music with funk, hip-hop and jazz to create an unmistakable sound rooted in the city’s rich musical heritage. Their infectious grooves and uplifting performances have made them festival favourites around the world.

data.name: W.I.T.C.H.
data.body: Widely recognised as pioneers of Zamrock, W.I.T.C.H. helped shape a groundbreaking fusion of rock, psychedelia and traditional African influences in 1970s Zambia. Decades after their formation, the band continues to captivate audiences with their infectious rhythms, timeless songs and remarkable story of musical revival.

data.name: PVA
data.body: PVA are a London trio making high-intensity electronic music that sits between live band chaos and club-night release. Blending post-punk attitude with techno, electro and rave influences, their sound is tense, hypnotic and built for movement. Known for sweat-drenched, late-night energy and immersive performances, PVA turn every stage into a dark, ecstatic dancefloor.

data.name: Alabaster DePlume
data.body: Saxophonist, composer and poet Alabaster DePlume is celebrated for his deeply expressive music that blends jazz, spoken word and improvisation. His performances are intimate, uplifting and thought-provoking, creating powerful connections with audiences through empathy and creativity

data.name: Sophia Stel
data.body: Sophia Stel crafts intimate, emotionally resonant songs that blend indie-pop sensibilities with thoughtful songwriting. Her captivating voice and honest storytelling have quickly earned attention as one of Ireland’s promising emerging artists.

data.name: Maruja
data.body: Manchester’s Maruja are a visceral, boundary-pushing force blending post-punk, jazz, noise and spoken-word intensity into something totally their own. Known for explosive live shows that swing between chaos and control, their music feels urgent, political and deeply human. Expect jagged riffs, hypnotic grooves and performances that hit like a release valve for everything bottled up.

data.name: Sassy 009
data.body: Norwegian artist Sassy 009 creates dreamy electronic pop infused with ambient textures, delicate melodies and introspective lyricism. Her immersive soundscapes have established her as a distinctive voice within contemporary electronic music.

data.name: Seamus Fogarty
data.body: Seamus Fogarty is an Irish singer-songwriter known for his off-kilter blend of folk storytelling, electronics and dry, imaginative humour. His songs twist everyday observations into something surreal and strangely beautiful, drifting between acoustic warmth and glitchy experimentation. With a quietly captivating live presence, Fogarty brings a thoughtful, left-field set that rewards close listening.

data.name: The New Eves
data.body: Brighton-based quartet The New Eves create immersive, boundary-pushing music that blends folk traditions, experimental sounds and raw punk energy. Their captivating performances combine rich harmonies and fearless creativity to deliver something entirely unique.

data.name: Black Nylon
data.body: Dublin band Black Nylon fuse post-punk, electronic textures and dark pop influences into a sound that is both atmospheric and urgent. Their bold, genre-blurring approach has quickly established them as one of Ireland’s most intriguing emerging acts.

data.name: The Orchestra (For Now)
data.body: The Orchestra (For Now) are a London collective blending indie songwriting with bold, orchestral arrangements and a restless experimental edge. Their sound moves between intimacy and scale, building from delicate moments into sweeping, cinematic crescendos. On stage, they feel fluid and alive, a shifting wave of sound that pulls the crowd with it.

data.name: Gently Tender
data.body: Gently Tender are a British indie band formed by Palma Violets members Sam Fryer, Pete Mayhew and Will Doyle, alongside guitarist Adam Brown and formerly Celia Archer of The Big Moon. They make laid-back, detail-rich indie that drifts between folk warmth and left-field alternative sounds. Built on instinct, texture and a quiet emotional pull, their music feels loose but intentional, full of space and subtle hooks.

data.name: The Itch
data.body: The Itch are a London-based electronic outfit crafting sleek, high-impact club music with a sharp indie edge and a restless sense of energy. Blending driving rhythms, hypnotic textures and emotionally charged vocals, their sound sits somewhere between underground dancefloor tension and widescreen festival release. Known for immersive live sets that build, twist and explode in all the right moments, The Itch bring a pulse that cuts through day or night.

data.name: Hank
data.body: HANK combines indie-rock influences with sharp songwriting and an energetic live presence. Blending catchy melodies with heartfelt lyricism, the project continues to build momentum as one of Ireland’s exciting new musical voices.

data.name: Little Grandad
data.body: Little Grandad are a UK indie outfit blending playful storytelling with raw, guitar-driven energy and a streak of offbeat humour. Their sound jumps between jangly hooks, scrappy charm and unexpectedly heartfelt moments.

data.name: George Houston
data.body: Singer-songwriter George Houston combines honest lyricism with a distinctive voice and contemporary folk-pop sensibilities. His heartfelt songs and engaging stage presence have earned him a growing reputation as one of Ireland's promising new talents.

data.name: Sell Everything
data.body: Sell Everything fuse post-punk attitude, experimental textures and sharp songwriting into a sound that is both unpredictable and compelling. Their energetic performances and creative approach have made them a standout among Ireland’s emerging alternative acts.

data.name: Cable Boy
data.body: Cable Boy fuses indie-rock energy with witty lyricism and infectious melodies, delivering songs that are equal parts thoughtful and exhilarating. Their vibrant live shows and fresh approach to songwriting have helped them stand out as one of Ireland's exciting emerging acts.

data.name: BABYRAT
data.body:
Bursting through the heart of Cork City, BABYRAT is cutting through the noise with razor-sharp riffs, anthemic choruses and the kind of edge that power-pop has been missing.

Their self-proclaimed ‘bitch-pop’ sound has sonically landed the bright-eyed five somewhere between The Strokes and Olivia Rodrigo, a sound which they have taken from local bars to arenas in just one year since forming in late 2024.

data.name: DOG SWIM
data.body: Dublin outfit Dog Swim craft energetic indie-rock packed with driving melodies, heartfelt lyricism and infectious charm. Their dynamic live performances and growing catalogue of standout releases have made them a rising force on Ireland's independent music scene.

data.name: Echo North Star
data.body: Irish songwriter Echo Northstar creates immersive soundscapes that blend indie, alternative and atmospheric influences into a captivating live experience. With thoughtful songwriting and expansive arrangements, their music balances introspection with powerful moments of release.

data.name: My First Time
data.body: Dublin-based duo My First Time bring together electronic production, alternative pop and infectious energy to create a sound that is playful, modern and impossible to pin down. Their vibrant performances have quickly made them a standout name on Ireland’s emerging music scene.

data.name: Takuya Nakamura (Live)
data.body: Originally from Tokyo, Japan, trumpeter, producer and composer Takuya Nakamura blends jazz, electronic music and experimental sounds into a vibrant and innovative live experience. A longtime collaborator across New York’s underground music scene, his performances showcase exceptional musicianship and creative exploration.

data.name: Byrne's Night
data.body: David Byrne’s Night is a collaborative, cult live project celebrating the music of David Byrne and Talking Heads, reimagined by a rotating cast of some of the most exciting artists in the UK and Irish alternative scene. Blending live performance, improvisation and a shared love of iconic songwriting, it’s part tribute, part chaos, part late-night festival ritual. Expect big moments, unexpected collaborations and a dancefloor energy that never lets up.

data.name: RIP Magic
data.body: RIP Magic craft vibrant, genre-defying music that draws from electronic, alternative and pop influences. Their adventurous sound and energetic live shows have helped establish them as one of Ireland’s most exciting new acts.

data.name: Fio Fa
data.body: Dublin-based selector Fio Fa is known for weaving together eclectic sounds from across the electronic spectrum. Blending deep grooves, leftfield discoveries and infectious rhythms, her sets create a vibrant atmosphere that keeps crowds locked in from start to finish.

data.name: Denver Cuss
data.body: Denver Cuss is a UK-based singer crafting a rich, nostalgic sound that blends classic R&B, soul and vintage pop influences with a modern edge. Built around warm, emotive vocals and lush, retro-inspired arrangements, their music draws on the spirit of 60s soul and mid-century songwriting while keeping a fresh, contemporary feel. With a deep love of groove, harmony and timeless melodies, Denver Cuss brings a smooth, transportive energy to the stage.

data.name: Mount Pyrus
data.body:
Once you’ve caught a glimpse, it’s hard not to become captivated by the weird and wonderful world of Mount Pyrus. What started as a retro-pop, indie-jazz inspired dream project has morphed beyond just music. Their unique combination of genres, visuals and samples creates a universe that explores psychedelia, nature and space, inviting listeners to travel through it all.

The band’s sound is brought to life by retro synth lines, soft vocals, groovy bass and driving drums. Immersive samples, soundscapes and visuals create an experience for the audience and piece together a unique and playful live show.

For fans of Crumb, Men I Trust and Mild High Club

data.name: Derv
data.body: A respected figure within Ireland's electronic community, Derv is known for expertly crafted sets that move effortlessly through house, techno and underground club sounds. Expect deep grooves, impeccable selections and dancefloor-focused energy.

data.name: Kelly Anne Byrne 'Prince Tribute'
data.body: Broadcaster, DJ and lifelong Prince devotee Kelly-Anne Byrne celebrates the music of one of pop's greatest innovators. Expect a journey through Prince's legendary catalogue, from timeless classics to hidden gems, packed with funk, soul, groove and pure Purple Rain energy.

data.name: David Jackson
data.body: David Jackson blends contemporary club sounds with timeless influences, his sets are packed with groove, atmosphere and momentum.

data.name: MOIO
data.body: MOIO is a Nigerian-Irish singer, songwriter and producer based in Dublin, known for blending bedroom pop, alt-R&B and indie influences into emotionally rich, genre-blurring songs. With warm melodies, intimate production and a gift for capturing vulnerability in sharp, modern detail, his music moves between understated reflection and widescreen feeling. Fast emerging as one of Ireland’s most compelling new voices, MOIO’s live sets bring a quiet intensity that pulls audiences in and holds them there.

data.name: Maykay
data.body: MayKay is an Irish singer, songwriter and performer known for her electrifying presence and unmistakable voice. Rising to prominence as frontwoman of Fight Like Apes and later Le Galaxie, she has become one of Ireland’s most dynamic live artists, moving effortlessly between indie, electronic and alternative worlds. Whether fronting a stage, collaborating across the Irish music scene, or going solo, MayKay brings bold energy, sharp wit and pure performance power every time.

data.name: Hot Chip (DJ Set)
data.body: Beyond their status as one of Britain's most beloved electronic bands, Hot Chip are also renowned selectors with an encyclopaedic knowledge of dance music. Their DJ sets are playful, eclectic and packed with everything from house and disco to unexpected dancefloor gems.

data.name: Burt Bacharach by Paddy Hanna
data.body: Irish singer-songwriter Paddy Hanna pays homage to the legendary songwriter Burt Bacharach. This musical project includes live performances and a double single featuring covers of "What's New Pussycat?" and "Walk On By," released via Strange Brew.

data.name: Brunch on The bandstand with Tony Cantwell
data.body:
GIVE IT A LASH TALENT SHOW
Come along and test out your talents with your host Tony Cantwell. Featuring prizes, special guests, and more. Crack open a soft drink, and come enjoy the show!

data.name: Getdown Edits
data.body: Get Down Edits is an Irish house and disco production and DJ duo formed in Waterford, Ireland by Darren "Daz" Dalton and Martin Roche. Known for their crate-digging roots and re-edits of classic funk and soul, they have released several highly regarded EPs and run their own boutique label.

data.name: Last Apollo
data.body: Last Apollo is the performing name of Irish-born, London-based artist and composer Lucy Rice. She blends pop, rock, and classical music to create a unique sound.

data.name: Mercorn
data.body:
Mercorn, the Dublin-based DJ and member of collectives Tender and Skin&Blister, is a force in Ireland’s rave scene. With a passion for hard house, prog, and trance, her sets are defined by soaring basslines, giddy snare rolls, and euphoric energy, capturing the essence of 90s Irish rave culture. Mercorn has gained recognition across the UK and Europe, playing at iconic queer parties like Adonis and Big Dyke Energy in London, as well as top venues in Ireland such as Wigwam and Yamamori Tengu.

Beyond DJing, Mercorn is an active community builder. Through Skin&Blister, she champions female, trans, and non-binary creatives, helping diversify Ireland’s male-dominated club scene. As co-founder of Tender, she hosts inclusive, raucous queer parties in Dublin, promoting local and international talent. Mercorn is also a talented designer, running MNW Design, where she handcrafts acclaimed clothing. A true multi-disciplinary artist, she blends music, design, and community.

data.name: Bull Horris
data.body: Bull Horris is a DJ and artist, whose work has moved through sound in varying forms over the past number of years. Co-founder and resident of TENDER, a nomadic (by necessity), queer DIY party, based in Dublin, they create intentional spaces and dancefloors for the community. Playing mostly vinyl their sets have a retrospective approach, with sometimes sexy, oftentimes camp vocals to the forefront and chord progressions that reminisce on that distinctly Euro sound. Bull Horris is driven by a love for the dancefloor and the cathartic moments it can bring.

data.name: Lúnasa
data.body:
Lúnasa is a DJ and producer that packs a punch. She is a well loved regular on the Irish club circuit and afar playing venues such as Yamamori Tengu (IE), Wigwam (IE), The Black Box (NI), The Vic (SL) and Sneaky Pete’s (EDI). Lúnasa runs her own DIY club night, Stretch and FLINTA electronic music skill share, Meitheal. Renowned for her technical precision, Lúnasa's sets are drum centric and daring, showcasing her flair for finding subtle sound links that create fearless genre blends that spur dynamic, emotional, and joyous dance floor moments. By combining the bleeding ends of multiple uplifting and introspective club-focused sounds, Lúnasa’s sets strive towards synergistic body music.

Lúnasa’s productions are rooted in global rhythms and hard drum with crisp melodies, catchy vocals and assertive bass lines. Her debut SAOR EP and track ‘Change’ (Funky Adjacent, UK) have gained support from the likes of RHONI, Burna and Shampain. Recent releases include labels such as Air Texture (USA), Ethereal Skies (IE), Reasons to Dance (IE) and Funky Adjacent (UK). Forthcoming music in 2026 will be released on Flood (IE). 

Through Lúnasa’s DIY club night Stretch, she is committed to giving underrepresented talent the set they deserve. Born out of the unquantifiable experience of collective effervescence on the dance floor and the unique sense of journey created during all night long sets, Stretch welcomes the community to a bi monthly dj extravaganza set.

data.name: Mabfield Live Podcast with Getdown Services
data.body:
Join Mabfield co-founder and music journalist Dylan Murphy for a live conversation with Getdown Services. The duo have built a cult following with their brilliantly offbeat blend of dance punk and spoken word. They head for an hour long conversation about their journey ahead of their Sunday performance.
Through long form conversations, Dylan goes beyond the usual promo cycle to uncover the lore that often falls between the cracks, shining a light on the people and stories shaping music culture today.

data.name: Flynn Johnson
data.body: Dublin artist Flynn Johnson translates his environment and experiences into sharp storytelling and precise rhyme schemes. His debut album, THE GREEN BOX THEORY, traces the “children of the hill” who learn to find beauty in a place others tend to call broken. Described by Johnson as “a love letter to the estate and a thank-you note for the lessons it taught me”, the album moves between themes of bravado, sorrow and survival. Praised for his “unfiltered storytelling and profound societal insight”, Johnson uses music to document local memory and share it with others, one carefully written verse at a time.

data.name: Delivery Service
data.body:
Delivery Service is an alternative rock band from Dublin, Ireland. Drawing inspiration from 90s female-fronted bands like The Breeders, The Sundays & Le Tigre the band blends punchy basslines, distorted guitars, and sweet vocal harmonies to create a sound that’s both unique and nostalgic.

Since forming, Delivery Service have played Left of the Dial fest in Rotterdam, Ireland Music Week, Other Voices, All Together Now and have opened for bands such as Far Caspian & Kean Kavanagh. The band released their debut single, “Ghost,” recorded with Aaron Corcoran (Skinner), in March 2025, the single has over 70k streams and was featured in several Spotify editorial playlists as well as several write ups in The Goo, Nialler9 and Genuine Irish.

data.name: SOAK
data.body: Derry-born singer-songwriter Bridie Monds-Watson (they/them; aka SOAK – a portmanteau of Soul and Folk) started writing songs at the tender age of thirteen, recording their first batch of lo-fi, acoustic demos in secret. Having uploaded an early demo of self-penned standout “Sea Creatures” to the BBC Introducing player in 2012, SOAK was soon hailed as one of the rising stars in Northern Ireland. Featured on the long list of BBC Sound of 2015, their official debut album Before We Forgot How To Dream won the Choice Prize in Ireland, the Northen Ireland Music Prize and was nominated for the Mercury Music Prize, After 2019’s Grim Town, SOAK recently returned with third album If I Never Know You Like This Again, released in May 2022. Recorded with long-time collaborator Tommy McLaughlin (he/him) and SOAK’s band in Donegal, McLaughlin & Monds-Watson wrote most of the album together while listening obsessively to indie greats like Broken Social Scene and Pavement (plus Radiohead’s classic album The Bends). Essentially “nerding out on guitars and pedals like moronic bros,” the result closes the gap between the mid-90s and the summer of ’22. It’s the kind of music that wouldn’t feel out of place in the end credits of a 90s coming-of-age film.

data.name: Freak Slug
data.body: The project of Xenya Genovese, Freak Slug blends dreamy indie, grunge, shoegaze and alt-pop into a sound that's nostalgic, playful and unapologetically unconventional. Fresh from the release of her acclaimed debut album I Blow Out Big Candles and a run of major UK, European and US festivals, she's quickly becoming one of indie's most exciting new live acts.

data.name: Ms Dynamite
data.body: Mercury Prize-winning singer, songwriter and rapper Ms. Dynamite burst onto the scene with her landmark debut A Little Deeper, becoming one of the UK's most influential voices in R&B, hip-hop and garage. Known for blending sharp social commentary with soulful vocals and infectious beats, her acclaimed catalogue and powerful live performances have cemented her status as a true icon of British music.

data.name: Mango
data.body: A stalwart of the Dublin nightlife scene, Mango commands the decks with an eclectic fusion of soulful Disco, driving House, and the high-speed bounce of Miami Bass. Widely regarded as a "selector’s selector," he pairs technical precision with an uncanny ability to read any room. As the founder of the influential Kumar Klub and the creative force behind the longstanding "Mango & Friends" nights, he has curated legendary parties across the city's iconic clubs and major festivals alike. His deep knowledge of the crates is further showcased as the host of the Smoke Breaks & Handbrakes radio show, where he explores the outer edges of his record collection. Blending razor-sharp mixing with signature Northside energy, Mango doesn't just play tracks—he builds communities on the dance floor, cementing his status as an essential architect of the Irish circuit.

data.name: ANZ
data.body: MOBO Award-nominated DJ and producer Anz is renowned for her electrifying, genre-blurring sets that weave together UK rave, techno, garage, breakbeats and bass with infectious energy. A regular at the world's biggest clubs and festivals, she has become one of the most exciting and forward-thinking names in electronic music.

data.name: JIO
data.body: New York-born, Dublin-based DJ Jio is the founder of the acclaimed club night Supper and a passionate champion of Ireland's underground electronic scene. Known for his eclectic, crate-digging approach, his sets effortlessly blend club music's past and present, earning him appearances on NTS Radio, Rinse FM and dancefloors across Ireland and beyond.

data.name: Mabfield Live Podcast with Maruja
data.body:
Join Mabfield co-founder and music journalist Dylan Murphy for a live conversation with Maruja. Together they'll explore the stories, influences and process behind one of the most exciting UK acts right now ahead of their performance at The Circle by Jameson Music.
Through long form conversations, Dylan goes beyond the usual promo cycle to uncover the lore that often falls between the cracks, shining a light on the people and stories shaping music culture today.

data.name: Cushla
data.body: Cushla is formed by Marc Fernández (electronics, production), Leo Pearson (production, electronics), and Nell Ní Chroinín (vocals, sean-nós). Together, they weave a unique sound that reimagines Ireland’s musical legacy through the fusion of sean-nós singing, traditional Irish instruments, and cutting-edge electronic production.

data.name: One Leg One Eye
data.body: One Leg One Eye is the drone-doom-folk project of founding Lankum member Ian Lynch and veteran noise artist George Brennan. Fusing traditional Irish music with haunting drones, experimental soundscapes and heavy atmospherics, the duo create immersive performances that push folk music into bold and uncharted territory.

data.name: Pebbledash
data.body: Cork's Pebbledash have quickly emerged as one of Ireland's most exciting new bands, crafting immersive songs that blend indie, folk and experimental rock. Fresh from acclaimed EPs, major European festival appearances and a feature in Netflix's House of Guinness, they're fast becoming one of the country's essential live acts.

data.name: Cromby
data.body: Irish-born, Berlin-based DJ and producer Cromby has become a leading force in underground electronic music, known for his infectious blend of house, techno and acid. With acclaimed releases on labels including Phantasy, Life and Death and his own Potency imprint, plus appearances at Berghain, Panorama Bar, Club Space Miami and festivals worldwide, he's established himself as one of the scene's most exciting selectors and producers.

data.name: Or:la
data.body: Derry-born DJ, producer and label head Or is one of electronic music's most distinctive voices, known for her genre-defying sound and adventurous approach to club culture. A former BBC Radio 1 resident with an Essential Mix and DJ Mag's Best DJ award to her name, she continues to push boundaries through her productions, labels and celebrated La Potion party series.

data.name: ÓIR
data.body:
ÓIR is a Dublin-based DJ and radio host with a sound rooted in late-90s and early-00s house. Her selections move through dubby, rolling tech house, bringing an old-school feel to the dancefloor. 

Alongside DJing, she hosts a monthly show on Dublin Digital Radio, curating an hour of club-focused hidden gems.

data.name: pôt-pot
data.body: Blending krautrock, psychedelia and hypnotic drone, Irish-Portuguese quintet pôt-pot craft immersive, groove-driven soundscapes that are as atmospheric as they are propulsive. Following acclaimed EPs, sold-out shows and the release of their debut album, they've quickly become one of the most exciting acts to emerge from Ireland's underground scene.

data.name: MIKE
data.body: New Jersey-born rapper and producer MIKE is one of the defining voices of modern underground hip-hop, celebrated for his introspective lyricism, soulful production and influential DIY approach. From shaping New York's underground scene to performing at Coachella and Primavera, his emotionally rich, self-produced music has cemented him as one of rap's most vital and innovative artists.

data.name: Rory Sweeney (Live)
data.body: Dublin-based producer Rory Sweeney crafts boundary-pushing electronic music that blends intricate production with a fiercely DIY spirit. A central figure in Ireland's thriving underground scene, his acclaimed 2025 album Old Earthcemented his reputation as one of the country's most innovative and uncompromising artists.

data.name: Jamz Supernova
data.body: DJ, broadcaster and Future Bounce label head Jamz Supernova is one of the UK's most influential tastemakers, renowned for championing cutting-edge underground music. From her award-winning BBC Radio 6 Music show to festival stages around the world, her genre-spanning sets effortlessly blend broken beat, UK funky, bass, techno and beyond.

data.name: Rahann
data.body: Chicago-born DJ and producer Rahaan is a true house and disco legend, celebrated for his deep crates, flawless mixing and timeless dancefloor selections. A key figure in Chicago's underground scene since the late '80s, his groove-rich sets and acclaimed productions continue to inspire dancers and DJs around the world.

data.body:

It’s time to ditch the old Gods and embrace the cultural revolution of colour, carnival and chaos. Frivolous entertainment melts serious culture, we blur the lines, blur the vision and refocus on a fantastical, art soaked future.

data.body: Dublin DJ and promoter Pablo is a key figure in Ireland’s disco and house scene, known for bringing international legends like Mr. Fingers, Lil Louis and Nicky Siano to Ireland for the first time. A respected selector and label head of Fatty Fatty Phonographics, he champions timeless disco, funk and house through his releases, residencies and celebrated all-day parties.

data.name: Odhrán
data.body: Odhrán is a DJ from Dublin specialising in Disco, Italo, and all funky cosmic things in between. Expect an anything goes approach to mixing with a playful selection of deep disko cuts throughout.

data.name: Gaff E
data.body: Hi-Energy Punk Disco Gremlin Gaff E is unapologetic in her bodily animal energy, as infamous as she is dedicated to colour and female vibrance. Her radical performances are a wild, carnal, hallucinogenic, activating trip! A shameless wild woman and chameleon of style liberating bodies everywhere. Gaff-E has performed and DJ’d around the world touring the global queer and cosmic scenes for many many moons. Gaff E thrives on sharing luscious performances and happy music to connect people with their true selves and ultimate freedom.

data.name: Franz Scala
data.body: Berlin-based Italian DJ and Slow Motion label head Franz Scala is known for eclectic, high-energy sets blending Italo disco, proto-house, acid and electro. A fixture in Berlin’s underground scene, he has released on respected labels and built a global reputation for his nostalgic yet forward-thinking approach to dance music.

data.name: DJ SexyT
data.body: Dublin-based DJ SexyT (SexyTadhg) is known for high-energy, genre-blending sets that fuse house, disco, techno and pop into euphoric, inclusive dancefloor experiences. A rising name in Dublin’s queer club scene, they are also co-founder of Big Fat Slut, a residency celebrating freedom, self-expression and community on the dancefloor.
