data.name: Sheriff
data.body: Sheriﬀ blurs the lines between alternative rock, pop and electronic music, crafting a sound that’s playful, bold and impossible to pin down. The Berlin-born and -raised singer uses her production to explore the boundaries between genres, through unconventional instrumentation, punchy guitars, catchy synth hooks and tongue-in-cheek lyrics with no regrets. Fans of Wetleg, Charli xcx or Getdown Services should see what Sheriﬀ has to oﬀer!

data.name: Pippa Molony
data.body:
Pippa Molony is an exciting electronic act from Dublin. Her debut EP, Hungry Ghost (October 2024), is an eight-track avant-pop EP that explores consumption, folklore and dreams, and was created in collaboration with producer Rory Sweeney. Her music nods to artists such as Sinéad O’Connor, Jenny Hval, Jockstrap, Astrid Sonne, Róis, Rachael Lavelle, Tirzah, Lankum and Bjork, while establishing a distinctly Irish, dark ethereal and otherworldly sonic identity of her own.
More recently, Pippa released a synth driven, atmospheric cover of the Irish rebel song The Foggy Dew (March 2026, feat. Rory Sweeney). The track marks her first release since Hungry Ghost and the beginning of a new body of work, with further releases planned throughout 2026.  
Her music has been featured by magazines such as Anois Os Aird, Hot Press, District Magazine, The Thin Air and Fourth Best to name a few, with radio play in Ireland and abroad. In 2025, she was named a Hot Press ‘Hot for 25’ artist, and her EP Hungry Ghost found itself in multiple end of year round ups (David Kitt/New Jackson’s Favourite Songs of 2024 for Nialler 9,The Thin Air’s Top 100 Irish Releases of 2024, and more)

data.name: Efa O'Neill
data.body: Efa O’Neill has spent the past decade immersed in the Irish electronic music scene. From her beginnings in Kerry, her sound has travelled through clubs, festivals and late-night dancefloors across Ireland, London, Ibiza and New York. Her sets are driven by groove, tension and contrast – deep rhythms, weighty bass, crisp percussion and unexpected turns flowing  between house, techno and bass.

data.name: Altern-8
data.body: Altern 8 is a British electronic music act, comprising Mark Archer and Chris Peat, until Peat left the group in 1994. Best known in the early 1990s, their trademark was electronic rave music with a heavy bass line.

data.name: Eats Everything
data.body: Daniel Pearce, better known as Eats Everything, is an English DJ and record producer. He came to prominence in 2011 with the release of "Entrance Song" on Pets Recordings. Since then, he has received critical acclaim for a number of solo releases on Dirtybird, Hypercolour and Futureboogie.

data.name: GRÁ
data.body: Grá is a Dublin collective reimagining Irish traditional music through a fresh, contemporary lens. Blending folk roots with modern influences and a collaborative spirit, they create immersive performances that celebrate tradition while boldly pushing it into new territory.

data.name: Sunil Sharpe x Kev Freeney Presents Spineless
Anish Kumar
data.body: Blending soulful house, breakbeats and South Asian influences, Anish Kumar has become one of the UK's most exciting electronic artists. Known for his uplifting productions and infectious DJ sets, expect warm grooves, euphoric energy and a dancefloor built for feel-good moments.

data.name: Floorplan
data.body: Floorplan is the father-daughter duo of Robert and Lyric Hood, fusing Detroit techno with uplifting house, disco and gospel influences. Renowned for their joyful, soul-stirring sets, they transform every dancefloor into a celebration of rhythm, connection and pure energy.

data.name: Peach
data.body: Canadian-born, UK-based DJ and producer Peach is renowned for her joyful, genre-spanning sets that blur the lines between house, techno, breaks and beyond. A favourite at clubs and festivals worldwide, she brings infectious energy, impeccable selections and feel-good moments to every dancefloor.

data.name: Sophie McAlister
data.body: Sophie McAlister is a boundary-pushing DJ and deep selector known for her genre-spanning sets that move effortlessly between house, disco, jungle, bass and techno. With a passion for digging deep and a fearless approach to mixing, she creates immersive dancefloor journeys filled with unexpected gems, emotion and energy.

data.name: Dan Shake
data.body: Dan Shake is a master of feel-good dance music, blending disco, house, funk and soulful grooves into unforgettable DJ sets. With infectious energy and impeccable selections, he keeps dancefloors moving from start to finish, delivering pure joy with every track.

data.name: Spray
data.body: Irish-born, Berlin-based DJ and producer Spray brings a hypnotic blend of progressive house, trance, breaks and psychedelic club sounds. Known for digging deep into the past while pushing forward with futuristic rhythms, his immersive sets deliver euphoric grooves, cosmic energy and unexpected twists on the dancefloor.

data.name: EMA
data.body: EMA brings a fearless blend of bass, breaks and leftfield club sounds, weaving together hypnotic rhythms and high-impact energy. With a genre-spanning approach and an instinct for unexpected moments, every set is a deep dive into the cutting edge of underground dance music.

data.name: DJ Nobu
data.body: A true icon of Japan's underground scene, DJ Nobu is renowned for his deep, hypnotic and ever-evolving sets. Blending techno, ambient and experimental sounds with effortless precision, he creates immersive journeys that have made him one of the world's most respected selectors.

data.name: Matcha
data.body: MATCHA brings a playful blend of house, progressive grooves and deep Italo influences to the dancefloor. Known for left-field selections, cosmic energy and effortlessly fun sets, MATCHA crafts vibrant journeys that keep crowds locked in from start to finish.

data.name: DIEBYVEG
data.body: DIEBYVEG is one of Ireland's rising electronic selectors, blending UK garage, deep house and bass-heavy club sounds into high-energy sets. With a fearless, genre-spanning approach and a distinct queer influence, expect infectious rhythms, big vibes and dancefloor euphoria from start to finish.

data.name: Soichi Terada (Live)
data.body: A pioneer of Japan’s electronic music scene, Soichi Terada is celebrated for his joyful take on deep house, blending soulful grooves, playful melodies and warm analogue sounds. Active since the late ’80s, his timeless productions and legendary DJ sets have earned him global recognition, with his unique fusion of house, jungle and experimental influences captivating dancefloors worldwide.

data.name: Gabrielle Kwarteng
data.body: Gabrielle Kwarteng is celebrated for her adventurous, genre-spanning DJ sets, effortlessly weaving together house, disco, techno and global rhythms. With impeccable taste and infectious energy, she creates dancefloor journeys that are both deeply soulful and irresistibly fun.

data.name: DJ Beks
data.body: Bekah Molony is a DJ, creative producer and tireless champion of Ireland's underground music scene. Known behind the decks as DJ BEKS, her sets are driven by feel-good energy, seamlessly weaving together soulful disco, house, R&B, global club sounds and bass-heavy rhythms. As the founder of Mo Cultivation and D07 Artists, she's spent years creating opportunities for emerging talent and building vibrant music communities. Whether she's on the airwaves, curating events or lighting up the dancefloor, Bekah brings an infectious passion for connection, culture and unforgettable parties.

data.name: Attention Bébé
data.body: Attention Bébé are a Dublin-based 16-piece party collective bringing the sounds of the ’90s to life with a high-energy mix of funk, dance, pop and mash-up madness. Known for their explosive live performances and feel-good approach, they transform familiar favourites into fresh, brass-fuelled anthems that keep crowds singing and dancing. With a sound built for big stages and unforgettable moments, Attention Bébé deliver a celebration of nostalgia, groove and pure festival energy.

data.name: Forget Romance
data.body: Forget Romance is an indie club night and DJ collective created by Olivia Chau and Shane Serrano, celebrating the best of alternative music from across the decades.

data.name: Graham Smyth
data.body: Graham Smyth is a broadcaster, DJ and lifelong music obsessive, known for bringing eclectic selections and infectious energy wherever he plays. A familiar voice on RTÉ 2FM and a regular at clubs and festivals across Ireland, his sets move effortlessly through house, disco, indie, electronic and unexpected gems, always with one goal in mind: keeping the dancefloor moving. Whether introducing listeners to new music on the airwaves or behind the decks, Graham's passion for great records shines through every set.

data.name: Onai
data.body: Onai is a vibe curator from Louth, now thriving in London’s club scene. Her sets seamlessly blend afrobeats, garage, house, and edits from deep cuts to festival-ready bangers, showcasing her uncanny ear for vibes and discovery.

data.name: Claire Beck's Sunday Revival
data.body: Claire Beck is one of Ireland's most respected broadcasters and DJs, renowned for her impeccable taste and deep passion for championing new music. A familiar voice on Irish radio, she's spent years introducing audiences to emerging artists while building a reputation for adventurous, genre-spanning DJ sets that move effortlessly from leftfield gems to dancefloor favourites. Whether behind the decks or behind the mic, Claire brings infectious energy, curiosity and an instinct for creating unforgettable musical moments.

data.name: Anna's Number
data.body: Anna's Number bring heartfelt indie rock to the stage with soaring melodies, honest songwriting and an effortless blend of intimacy and energy. Hailing from Belfast, the band craft emotionally rich songs that balance shimmering guitars with infectious hooks, drawing listeners into stories of love, change and self-discovery. Their debut EP, It Doesn't Have To Be Like This, showcases a confident sound that's both uplifting and deeply personal, marking them as one of Northern Ireland's exciting emerging acts.

data.name: Stevie G
data.body: Stevie G (Stephen Grainger) is one of Ireland's most respected DJs, broadcasters and tastemakers, with decades spent shaping the country's music scene. Renowned for championing hip-hop, soul, funk, house and Afro-influenced sounds, his dynamic sets are built on deep musical knowledge and an instinct for moving a crowd. As a long-time presenter on Cork's RedFM and a passionate advocate for emerging artists, Stevie G continues to inspire audiences on the airwaves, in clubs and at festivals across Ireland.

data.name: Shauna Dee
data.body: Shauna Dee is one of Ireland's fastest-rising electronic DJs, known for high-energy sets that blend house, techno and everything in between. A regular fixture across the country's clubs and festivals, she's built a reputation for fearless genre-hopping, slick mixing and an instinct for reading the dancefloor. Having shared line-ups with some of electronic music's biggest names, Shauna Dee brings infectious energy, driving rhythms and a party-first approach that's guaranteed to keep crowds moving.

data.name: D.O.T.S
data.body:
DOTS is an immersive outdoor festival performance celebrating community through dance, song, and storytelling. Inspired by the legend of Deirdre of the Sorrows, it explores the choices and consequences that lead to one of Ireland's most tragic tales.

Blending powerful movement, live music, and striking visual imagery, DOTS invites audiences to reconnect with timeless stories that reflect our shared humanity and their enduring relevance in today's world.

data.name: Magz
data.body: Magz will be mixing eclectic party bangers with disco euphoria. She'll deliver a stomping set, digging through timeless grooves, oddball gems, and undeniable dancefloor moments..

data.name: Paddy Steer
data.body: Paddy Steer is a one-man sonic adventurer, crafting colourful, unpredictable performances that blend analogue synthesis, experimental electronics and playful imagination. Equal parts cosmic, eccentric and captivating, his immersive live shows transform homemade instruments and inventive soundscapes into a truly unique musical experience.

data.name: Más Amor’s Sunday Service
data.body: The ultimate hangover cure is back! Más Amor’s Sunday Service returns for another year of glorious nonsense, hosted by international drag sensation Bridgette Fingers. Expect singalongs, sensational performances, and plenty of big gay fun at Ping Pong Disco. Artist duo Más Amor bring you all the best bits of church but without any of the guilt or religious nonsense to give your Sunday the fabulous kick-start it deserves.

data.name: DJ Transit b2b DJ Smallboy
data.body: DJ Transit goes back-to-back with DJ Small Boy for a Sunday afternoon set. Grab your whips and buckle up for one hell of a ride through the Wild Wild West—an afternoon of country classics, dusty trails and a fistful of country bangers.

data.name: Shrem
data.body: Shrem is a Dublin-based Polish queer blogger, vinyl selector, DJ and self-confessed über-nerd serving euphoric dancefloor escapism with flair. Known for wildly curated themed nights and gloriously eclectic sets, they weave together house, synth-pop, electro, italo, boogie and disco into a high-energy ride of certified bangers, forgotten gems, diva anthems and unapologetic guilty pleasures. For Ping Pong Disco, expect a one-afternoon-only glitterbomb of sequins, brocade, sweat and sparkle - a joyous Sunday dancefloor odyssey where every track serves belter realness.

Cian has never been called a genius.

 Music style is synth-heavy disco groove rhythms, with eclectic curve balls from around the world. From mellow, soulful & sweet disco bangers to Italo and electro late night chuggers. It's all about the dance floor and a deep love of music. 

Still never been called a genius.

data.name: Daniel Wang
data.body:
Daniel Wang has been involved in nightclubs and Dance Music for a very very long time now! He's originally from California, lived in New York in the 1990s, but he has been based in Berlin for over 23 years now.  He started going out to clubs in downtown New York in 1988, he played at Ostgut (the original Berghain) in 2001, and has been a regular DJ at every favorite club + party in Berlin, including the famous KitKat Club and Cocktail d'Amore. He still has a monthly residency at Paloma in Kreuzberg. In 2024-2025 he played in Amsterdam, Barcelona, Brussels, Sicily, Stockholm, Paris, a faraway beach in Brazil, and everywhere in Japan.. 

          His own releases and edits since 1993 on Balihu and Environ Records are still collected and played by DJs everywhere, including DJ Harvey and Moodyman; the recent massive Balihu re-issue from Rush Hour Records in 2026 sold out instantly.

But most importantly  - everyone knows this - Daniel Wang just loves to dance and have fun with people on the dancefloor!  He loves Salsoul and guitars and congas, he hates instagram selfies, commercial festivals with big stages, and boring laptop cut-and-paste techno.   He brings his joyful spirit and deep musicality to every gig.  Just come and have a great time with us at ATN 2026!!

data.name: Madonna Kebab
data.body:
Madonna Kebab aka the High Queen of Ulster and the biggest mouth in Derry is back and will be dishing out delectable disco, craic is whack talk, triple nip slips, mega mic drops, down low blows, high notes and fur coats of charms.

Bígi réidh, bígí gay agus bígí ag damhsa leis an Mhaighdean Ceibeab!

data.name: The Simpler Life? LIVE: The Renovation Rollercaster with James Kavanagh and William Murray
data.body: After a packed tent last summer, James & William are back with a special live edition of their hit podcast The Simpler Life? telling all about their country house renovation, the highs and lows, kitchen dreams and nightmares and the food and drink that is getting them through.

data.name: The Déise, Decanted: A Sunny South East Showcase with Dungarvan Brewing, Eunice Power, Fat Tomato & more
data.body: Join a bunch of proud locals and brilliant producers for a lively, flavour-first look at the food and drink coming out of Waterford, Wexford and beyond. Expect pours from Dungarvan Brewing, standout local cheese from Knockanore and a generous hit of Wexford’s finest produce from Anthony O’Toole’s Fat Tomato - with plenty of tasters and opinions along the way.

data.name: Sip Sip Hooray! Champagne Opening Party with Tara Deery and Sinéad McCarthy
data.body: We’re opening the stage with two of Ireland’s leading sommeliers, Sinéad McCarthy from Fíon Eile and Tara Deery as they unpack the world of Champagne - the myths, the makers, the magic and the marketing spins. Expect a bubbly tasting that separates substance from sparkle.

data.name: Whiskey on the Table with Oisín Davis
data.body: Join drinks expert and Cooking with Irish Whiskey author Oisín Davis for a lively, flavour-packed demo exploring how Irish whiskey works across the table, from clever food pairings to cocktails worth making at home. Expect big flavours, plenty of pours, and a bit of chaos along the way.

data.name: Frying Pan or Fire: Hot Takes with Dee Laffan, Kevin Thornton, Eric Matthews, Paul Flynn, Karl Cooney, Jordan Mooney & more
data.body: Get ready for some sizzling opinions as some of Ireland’s top names in food and drink share their hottest takes on restaurants, food or even customers, and you get to be the judge! Each foodie has 90 seconds to deliver their boldest, most controversial claim, making their case. (Will Kevin Thornton mention chips?) Then it’s over to the audience: whose take stays in the frying pan (totally valid) and who gets tossed into the fire (no way, move on!)?

data.name: I’ll Have What She’s Having: Iconic Rom Com Food and Drink with Hilary Quinn, Ali Dunworth, Louise McSharry, Jordan Mooney and Boatyard Distillery
data.body: Ever noticed the role food and drink play in romantic comedies? We have. From that famous Katz’s Deli scene to dishes that spark romance or soothe heartbreak, our esteemed panel of rom com fans will discuss the food and drink moments that are as big as the characters. With drinks!

data.name: An Ode to the Irish Chipper with Shamim de Brún, Melissa McCabe and Marcus O’Laoire
data.body: From its Italian-Irish roots to the eternal questions- batter or breadcrumbs, long tray or short, curry or garlic -  this is a celebration of one of the country’s great institutions. Join food writer Shamim de Brún, chef Melissa McCabe, and devoted chipper enthusiast Marcus O’Laoire as they get into spice burgers, perfect chips and why the chipper still hits like nothing else.

data.name: Bia Duit LIVE with Ann Marie Duffin and Shaun Lavelle
data.body: Journalist Shaun Lavelle in conversation with Ann Marie Duffin, better known as Bia Duit, to tell us all about the role of food in Irish summer folklore, focusing on Bealtaine and Lughnasa. From butter‑stealing spells, shared harvest food to matchmaking on hilltops.

data.name: Chocolate and Whiskey with Bean and Goose and Foxes Bow
data.body: Karen and Natalie Keane from Bean and Goose lead an interactive chocolate talk and tasting, where chocolate is anything but ordinary. Alice Carroll from Foxes Bow brings the whiskey spike. Stories, sips and serious craft from two brilliant Irish brands.

data.name: The Teddy Bears Picnic with Joanna Bourke Lawlor (family friendly)
data.body: Ballymaloe-trained cook Joanna Bourke Lawlor hosts a family-friendly version of her Savour Picnics, exploring how we think about and eat food, with drawing, imagination, food and fun. Interactive food fun for kids, adults and teddies.

data.name: K Pop Demon Hunter Instant Noodles with Aoife McElwain (family friendly)
data.body: Author of the Blasta cookbook, Messy, and host of Sing Along Social, Aoife McElwain, shows us how to create a dish inspired by one of her all-time favourite comfort films, K-Pop Demon Hunters and chats about how she turns chaos into craic in the kitchen and beyond

data.name: Bia agus Deoch: pop-up food & drink Gaeltacht with Ann Ní Chíobháin, Dáire Ó Lúing & Siobhan Ní Ghairbhith
data.body: A tasty pop-up Gaeltacht celebrating Irish food, drink and the people shaping it. Ann Ní Chíobháin of Cáis food truck and new Blasta book, sommelier Dáire Ó Lúing and Siobhán Ní Ghairbhith of St Tola goat’s cheese, one of the country’s finest producers and a proud Gaeilgeoir. Expect good food, great drink, and cupla focail from cheesemaking to wine lists, toasties to terroir.

data.name: Main Character Menus with Aishling Moore (Goldie), Sofie Rooney & Garret FitzGerald (Chimac) and Barry Wallace (Dash)
data.body: From fin-to-tail fish to cult fried chicken and smash burgers, some of Ireland’s most talked-about restaurants are built on one clear, compelling idea. But what turns a concept into a hit? Join the chefs and founders behind three standout spots as they unpack how these ideas take shape, how they’re executed, and what we love eating.

data.name: The New Irish Pour with Judith & Susan Boyle, Legacy Cider, Boatyard, Craft Cocktails, Foxes Bow, Karl Cooney & Fierce Mild
data.body: Publican, brewer and drinks educator Judith Boyle and drinks consultant, beverage researcher and award-winning drinks writer Susan Boyle introduce us to some of the most exciting Irish drinks right now, from Legacy Cider’s latest releases to Boatyard’s ready-to-pour mixes, Karl Cooney’s creations, Craft Cocktails and crisp non-alc lagers from Fierce Mild.

data.name: Taste Bud Time Machine: Food of the 80s and 90s with Erica Drum, Ciara Daly and guest chef JR Ryall
data.body: Step back into the flavours of the 80s and 90s for a taste of nostalgia as chef Erica Drum and foodie Ciara Daly get the audience to blind-taste iconic foods from decades past. Will we remember the foods that shaped us? Do they still taste as good? Guest chef JR Ryall brings treats to take us right back.

data.name: Both Sides of the Bar with Matt Smyth & Mike O'Connor (The Centre Cut Podcast) and Dave Taylor (The Sackville Lounge)
data.body: Matt Smyth and Mike O’Connor, hosts of The Centre Cut podcast, are joined by Dave Taylor of The Sackville Lounge for a lively look at modern classics. Expect top-notch cocktail-making, strong opinions and strong drinks.

data.name: The Kitchen Press Céilí: A Celebration of Theatre of Food - Sally & John McKenna, Derry Clarke, Kevin Thornton, Máirtín Mac Con Iomaire, Seáneen Sullivan & more
Cormac Leahy
data.body: Cormac Leahy is an Irish singer-songwriter whose music blends rich folk traditions with heartfelt storytelling and timeless melodies. Drawing inspiration from classic Americana, Celtic roots, and acoustic songwriting, his performances balance warmth, wit, and emotional depth.

data.name: Martello
data.body: Martello craft immersive indie-folk soundscapes that fuse soaring harmonies, atmospheric instrumentation, and deeply personal songwriting. Drawing influence from Ireland's rich musical heritage while embracing a modern, cinematic edge, the band create songs that feel both intimate and expansive.

data.name: Ndidi O
data.body: Ndidi O is an Irish-Nigerian artist whose music effortlessly blends soul, R&B, jazz, folk, and spoken word into a sound that's entirely her own. With rich, expressive vocals and deeply personal songwriting, she explores themes of identity, belonging, love, and resilience. Her captivating live performances combine warmth, honesty, and effortless musicality, creating an intimate connection with audiences. Powerful yet understated, Ndidi O is an artist whose voice and stories leave a lasting impression.

data.name: Raynor
data.body: Raynor is an Irish singer-songwriter crafting intimate indie-folk songs filled with heartfelt lyricism, rich melodies, and understated charm. Blending acoustic textures with honest storytelling, his music explores themes of love, change, and the moments that shape us. Whether performing stripped-back ballads or uplifting, full-bodied arrangements, Raynor brings a warmth and authenticity that draws listeners in.

data.name: Jodie Lyne
data.body: Jodie Lyne is an Irish singer-songwriter whose soulful voice and heartfelt songwriting blend folk, indie, and contemporary pop influences into an effortlessly captivating sound. With honest lyrics, melodic warmth, and an intimate performance style, her songs explore love, growth, and the complexities of everyday life.

data.name: Politik
data.body: Politik deliver an electrifying blend of indie rock, post-punk energy, and razor-sharp songwriting. Driven by infectious rhythms, powerful guitars, and emotionally charged vocals, the band balance raw intensity with memorable hooks and an unmistakable live presence. Their songs capture the urgency and unpredictability of modern life while inviting audiences to lose themselves in the moment.

data.name: The Awning
data.body: The Awning are an Irish indie-folk outfit weaving together lush harmonies, evocative songwriting, and beautifully textured arrangements. Blending elements of folk, alternative, and atmospheric pop, the band create songs that feel both deeply personal and universally resonant.

data.name: Harry Fennell
data.body: Harry Fennell is an Irish singer-songwriter whose heartfelt blend of folk, indie, and acoustic pop is driven by honest storytelling and memorable melodies. With a warm, expressive vocal and an effortless stage presence, his songs explore love, self-discovery, and the experiences that connect us all.

data.name: Trad session: Grá
data.body: Grá breathe new life into Ireland's rich traditional music with vibrant musicianship, infectious energy, and a deep respect for the tunes and songs that have shaped generations. Blending masterful instrumental performances with fresh arrangements and contemporary flair, the group create a sound that feels both rooted in tradition and excitingly modern.

data.name: Barnburner
data.body:
Barnburner are an emerging Dublin alt-folk duo that blends confessional lyricism and vocal harmonies with intricate guitar instrumentation. Their debut five-track EP, ‘Nothing to Hold’ was released on March 20, 2026 and has been described as an intimate, moving and atmospheric project rooted in both traditional folk storytelling and alternative sensibilities.
The duo, Pippa Molony (composer, lyricist) and David Mac Dhubháin (composer, lyricist, guitarist), Barnburner craft songs that balance intimacy and expansiveness. Their music nods to artists such as Phoebe Bridgers, Adrienne Lenker, Pinegrove, Slow Pulp, The Cranberries, and Alex G, while establishing a distinct, at times dark and brooding, whimsical and otherworldly sonic identity of their own.

data.name: Becca Colley
data.body: Becca Colley is an Irish singer-songwriter blending heartfelt lyricism, captivating vocals, and delicate musical arrangements to create a sound that feels both intimate and deeply expressive. Drawing from folk, indie, and contemporary influences, her songs explore themes of love, identity, and the moments that shape our lives.

data.name: Elishka Lane
data.body: Elishka Lane is an Irish singer-songwriter whose music blends soulful vocals, thoughtful songwriting, and emotive storytelling. Drawing inspiration from folk, indie, and contemporary pop influences, she creates songs that explore connection, vulnerability, and the complexities of everyday life.

data.name: Lemoncello
data.body: Lemoncello are an Irish folk duo blending intricate harmonies, poetic songwriting, and contemporary folk influences. With beautifully crafted melodies and a unique sense of intimacy, they create music that feels both timeless and fresh, capturing stories of connection, identity, and the human experience.

data.name: Dermot Henry
data.body: Dermot Henry is an Irish singer-songwriter blending heartfelt lyrics, warm vocals, and timeless melodies. Drawing from folk and acoustic traditions, his music captures moments of life, love, and reflection with honesty and charm, creating intimate performances that connect deeply with audiences.

data.name: Sun Studio Collective
data.body: Sun Studio Collective brings together a vibrant mix of musicians and creative voices, blending soulful sounds, rich harmonies, and a shared passion for collaboration. Their performances celebrate connection, creativity, and the joy of live music, creating an uplifting experience for audiences.

data.name: Annika Kilkenny
data.body: https://www.instagram.com/annika.kilkenny/?hl=en

data.name: KK Lewis
data.body: KK Lewis is an Irish singer-songwriter blending soulful vocals, heartfelt lyrics, and rich melodies. With influences spanning folk, indie, and contemporary songwriting, KK creates intimate performances filled with emotion, honesty, and connection.

data.name: T.A. Narrative
data.body: T.A. Narrative are a Limerick electro-pop duo blending pulsing synths, infectious hooks, live instrumentation, and post-punk energy. Formed by childhood friends Tara and Anna, their music combines bold production with dynamic storytelling and an unforgettable live presence.

data.name: Softdrink Millionaire
data.body: Softdrink Millionaire are a Bray-based alternative band blending hazy indie, playful experimentation, and raw DIY energy. With catchy hooks, unpredictable arrangements, and a distinctive live sound, they create music that feels both nostalgic and refreshingly original. Their performances capture the spirit of Ireland’s underground scene with plenty of personality, creativity, and charm.

data.name: Larabel
data.body: Larabel is a Donegal-born singer-songwriter blending ethereal indie, heartfelt storytelling, and atmospheric melodies. With a captivating voice and deeply personal songwriting, she creates music that feels both intimate and expansive, weaving together Irish influences with a fresh, contemporary sound.

data.name: Rua Rí
data.body: Rua Rí is a Cork singer-songwriter blending heartfelt storytelling, atmospheric melodies, and intimate indie-folk influences. With a thoughtful approach to songwriting and a deeply personal sound, his music explores themes of love, memory, and connection, creating performances that feel honest, immersive, and emotionally resonant.

data.name: Bayviin
data.body: BAYVIIN is an Irish alternative pop artist blending cinematic soundscapes, soaring melodies, and deeply emotive storytelling. With a captivating voice and atmospheric production, her music explores themes of connection, vulnerability, and human experience, creating an immersive sound that feels both intimate and expansive.

data.name: Roisín Gowen
data.body: Róisín Gowen is an Irish alt-folk singer-songwriter blending intimate storytelling, rich vocals, and beautifully crafted melodies. With a sound rooted in folk tradition and contemporary songwriting, her music explores love, loss, and resilience with honesty and emotional depth. Róisín’s captivating performances invite audiences into deeply personal stories of connection, reflection, and hope.

data.name: d_abdu
data.body: d_abdu is the solo project of Ethio-Irish musician Dara Abdurahman, blending lo-fi folk, indie, and experimental sounds with deeply personal songwriting. Drawing inspiration from raw emotion and intimate storytelling, his music creates a thoughtful, atmospheric world filled with honesty, vulnerability, and understated beauty.

data.name: County Rocket
data.body: County Rocket bring a fresh burst of energy to the Irish music scene with their distinctive sound, infectious melodies, and captivating live performances. Blending creative songwriting with a passion for connection and collaboration, they deliver music that is engaging, vibrant, and full of character. A rising act with plenty of personality, County Rocket are set to make their mark on the festival stage.

data.name: India Blue
data.body: India Blue is a contemporary Faerie-Folk musician and multi-instrumentalist based in the South East of England. Blending piano, harp, harmonium, and strings, she weaves tales of folklore, nature, and spirituality. She has gained a dedicated following for her deeply resonant, genre-blending sound.

data.name: Heron Red
data.body: Heron Red are a folk duo blending traditional Irish influences with Americana, country, and contemporary songwriting. With rich harmonies, heartfelt storytelling, and a full-band energy, their music moves between intimate acoustic moments and soaring, uplifting performances. Combining poetic lyrics with timeless melodies, Heron Red create a sound that feels both rooted and refreshingly modern.

data.name: Trad Session: Trá Pháidín
data.body: Trá Pháidín brings a wild and wonderful collision of Irish trad, jazz, post-rock, and spontaneous improvisation. Rooted in tradition but driven by experimentation, Trá Pháidín create a sound that is energetic, unpredictable, and completely their own.

data.name: Bulbs
data.body: Bulbs are bringing fresh energy, big personality, and a spark of creativity to the stage. With infectious melodies, playful spirit, and a sound that keeps listeners guessing, they deliver a live show full of colour, charm, and good vibes.

data.name: Ciúnas
data.body: Ciúnas are a Dublin indie band bringing infectious melodies, shimmering guitars, and bold storytelling to the Irish music scene. Blending classic songwriting with a fresh modern edge, their songs explore identity, connection, and the chaos of everyday life.

data.name: All Things Eve
data.body: All Things Eve is a singer-songwriter blending folk influences, intricate melodies, and deeply personal storytelling. With a captivating voice and a sound that moves between intimate acoustic moments and rich, atmospheric arrangements, Eve creates songs filled with emotion, vulnerability, and poetic beauty.

data.name: Tessio
data.body: Derry duo blending rich harmonies, heartfelt songwriting, and timeless acoustic melodies. With influences spanning folk, indie, and classic songcraft, Jude McCandless and Callum Feeney create music filled with warmth, honesty, and emotional depth.

data.name: Niamh Bury
data.body: Niamh Bury is one of the most captivating new voices in Irish folk music. Blending traditional influences with beautifully crafted original songs, her music is rich with poetic storytelling, haunting melodies, and a deeply distinctive vocal style.

data.name: Ailbhe Reddy
data.body: Ailbhe Reddy is a Dublin singer-songwriter known for her emotionally rich storytelling, distinctive vocals, and captivating blend of indie folk and alternative sounds. With deeply personal lyrics and beautifully crafted melodies, her music explores love, identity, and the complexities of human connection.

data.name: Black Turf
data.body: Black Turf blurs the lines between the old and new. Bending styles, borders and belief systems in song and spirit. Born from a generation of young Irish who struggle to remember and strive to redefine our country, our culture and ourselves in this post colonial world.

data.name: Vaticanjail
data.body: Vaticanjail has created her own world within Irish music that is getting noticed on the global stage; an immersive, dream-like experience that blends her Chilean roots, alternative electronic and contemporary dream-pop. After the release of the hit single ‘ANGEL’, followed by her debut EP SWEETS BAR now surpassing 200k streams, the world understood what Vaticanjail was all about, creating music to feel in your bones. Get ready to dance divas!

data.name: God Knows
data.body: One of the leading voices in Irish hip-hop, God Knows is celebrated for his fearless lyricism, commanding stage presence and pivotal role in shaping the country's thriving rap scene. A founding member of the award-winning group Rusangano Family and co-founder of the trailblazing narolane records, he's helped redefine the sound of modern Irish hip-hop while mentoring a new generation of artists. With acclaimed solo releases and praise from major music publications worldwide, God Knows continues to push boundaries with powerful performances and uncompromising creativity.

data.name: Celaviedmai
data.body:
Hailing from the west of Ireland, Celaviedmai’s music is revered for
its genre- blending across urban contemporary and electronic
sounds. Her lyrics move between English, French and Irish, paying
homage to her Ivory Coast heritage. Mai’s live performances set
her apart, delivering full band shows, live vocals and an
undeniable connection with audiences across Europe and the UK.
With long-awaited new music on the way and her explosive live
energy returning to stages throughout 2026, Celaviedmai is
entering her next era louder than ever.

data.name: Lullahush
data.body: Blending traditional Irish folk with forward-thinking electronic production, Lullahush creates a sound that's both deeply rooted and strikingly original. Weaving archival recordings, soaring melodies and club-ready rhythms into immersive live sets, the project reimagines Ireland's musical heritage for modern dancefloors. Ethereal, emotional and impossible to pin down, Lullahush offers a captivating journey where tradition and innovation collide.

data.name: RITHIM
data.body:
RITHIM is a pulsing mix of original afro-percussion and electronic dance floor beats with synth lines, samples and virtuosic live drumming.
A reinvention of Éamonn Cagney’s Rithim percussion band into a duo with tabla and udu player Ronan “Didgitaal” Skillen, and featuring an incredible special guest: Congolese fusion guitar maestro Niwel Tsumbu.
Expect the beat to go on and on, weaving the energy of club music with authentic and uplifting live drumming and guitaring from three of Ireland’s top music creators.

data.name: Dora Gola
data.body: Dora Gola is a Polish-born singer-songwriter and professional dancer based on the west coast of Ireland. Blending dark pop, Slavic folktronica, Eastern influences, ’80s funk grooves, and Irish trad elements, she creates a sound that is both cinematic and deeply immersive. Following acclaim from The Irish Times Magazine and Hot Press for her debut single Dark Sand, Dora released her debut album Dance With Danger in 2025. Her captivating live show combines haunting vocals, powerful dance, hypnotic beats, and striking visual storytelling.

data.name: Kez
data.body: Kez is an Irish artist from Dublin creating atmospheric music that blends folk, electronica, and alternative influences. Known for her distinctive voice, cinematic sound, and poetic lyrics - she explores themes of identity, nature, femininity, and solitude through emotionally rich compositions. With a growing reputation for captivating live performances and a unique artistic vision, Kez is emerging as one of Ireland's exciting new voices.

data.name: Paahto & The Bull
data.body: Paahto & The Bull is the guitar-duo project of Patrick "Paahto" Cummins and John Francis Flynn. Having met and played together since 2011 and having cut their teeth at The Maple Hotel on Dublin's Gardiner Street, Paahto and John helped form the Irish traditional group Skipper's Alley in 2013 and would remain long-term sparring partners and an integral cog in Dublin's traditional and folk music communities. Once There Was A King was another of their musical endeavours which reached into a progressive musical space in its short-lived timespan. However, as with any collaboration between these two players, Paahto & The Bull is beyond a meeting of two musical minds and encompasses a very personal element.

data.name: Trá Pháidín
data.body:
Trá Pháidín is a band that straddles a few different stools.
Between Connemara and Cork...
Between the Gaeltacht and the English-speaking world...
Between traditional music and jazz...
Between Krautrock and any other label that suits their marketing... maybe country music?
Having played gigs to date at Vicar Street, St. Luke's, the Sneem Summer Festival,
Ancienne Belgique, and Café OTO, the full Trá Pháidín lineup is returning to the Savoy this
summer to stir up a fine, entertaining, and distinctly Irish ruckus.

data.name: BoolaBoom
data.body: BoolaBoom are a 22 piece brass and percussion big band playing unplugged house music. Their set is a mix of original jazzed up high tempo belters and samba-infused reworks of EDM classics from the likes of St. Germain, Kerri Chandler, Faithless (Insomnia) and Moloko. So far this year they have played two sold out shows at the Savoy in Cork and the Sugar Club in Dublin and their latest track, a dark vocal called 'Too Much', was Dan Hegarty's Track of the Week on 2FM.

data.name: Yankari Afrobeat Collective
data.body:
Ireland’s premier Afrobeat orchestra.
Led by Nigerian composer and bandleader Segun Akano, Yankari combines Afrobeat, highlife, jazz and contemporary influences into one of Ireland’s most powerful live shows.
Rooted in the legacy of Fela Kuti, their music is rhythm-driven, politically aware and built for large audiences.
Rooted in the legacy of Fela Kuti, Yankari’s music carries the weight of that tradition without being defined by it — pushing the genre forward while keeping the groove at the centre of everything.

data.name: Felispeaks
data.body: FELISPEAKS is a Nigerian-Irish visionary artist celebrated for their profound exploration of identity, social justice, and personal growth through poetry, performance and theatre. Their work in ‘WAKE’ and ‘OCTOPUS CHILDREN’ has earned them both ‘Best Performer’ award in 2021 and Best Ensemble award in 2025 for Dublin Fringe Festival. FELISPEAKS returns to the festival stages with a band exploring a blend of sounds that honours their gospel roots, ancestral rhythms, jazz, drum and bass paired with poetry that frees both themselves and their audience. Their compelling work transcends borders, leaving an indelible mark on national and international stages.

data.name: AbbieLee
data.body:
Cork singer Abbie Lee is back at All Together Now, bringing her music to the Global Roots stage alongside good friend and skilled guitarist Leon Pino. Together, they’ll be serving up a chilled-out blend of neo-soul, trip-hop, and reggae favorites, mixed with a few of Abbie's own
original sounds. Having loved playing the festival in the past, they can’t wait to reconnect with the crowd and share their latest musical spin.

data.name: The Calvinists
data.body:
The Calvinists fuse alternative blues and gypsy spirit with a hint of circus mayhem into a sound full of grit, melody and heart.
Formed in 2010, the band made their mark with acclaimed live performances and the release of ‘Durango’ and ‘King of Lies’.
Now, after years away they are back writing and recording songs with a renewed energy.

data.name: Roisin El Cherif
data.body: Irish-Palestinian artist Róisín El Cherif creates spellbinding music that weaves together Irish and Arabic traditions with ethereal vocals, folklore and cinematic storytelling. Singing in English, Irish and Arabic, her work explores identity, heritage, love and belonging through a rich tapestry of myth, mysticism and haunting melodies. Drawing inspiration from both Irish mythology and her Palestinian roots, Róisín's captivating live performances offer a deeply moving journey across cultures and generations.

data.name: Qbanaa
data.body:
A Cuban-Irish singer-songwriter, Qbanaa fuses neo-soul, Latin jazz-
infused pop and raw storytelling with an effortless blend of classic and contemporary influences. Her sultry honey silk vocals, immersive sound and rich, multicultural heritage drive her mission to imprint Spanglish music on the global stage.

data.name: Toshín
data.body: Fronted by the powerhouse vocals of Tosin Bankole, Toshín are a six-piece soul outfit blending Motown grooves, modern R&B and infectious funk into an irresistible live show. From heartfelt ballads to high-energy dancefloor moments, their vibrant performances have lit up festivals across Ireland and seen them share stages with artists including Gregory Porter, Macy Gray and Corinne Bailey Rae. With acclaimed releases, sold-out headline shows and new music on the horizon, Toshín are one of Ireland's most exciting live acts.

data.name: Ar Ais Arís: Hannah Hession vs Rob Rua
data.body:
Rob Rua is a DJ based in Galway, Ireland. He is the co-founder and lead A&R at record labels Rua Sound, Foxy Jangle, and SPHERES with 26 vinyl releases under its belt. He is the founder of Ar Ais Arís, a west of Ireland based party and label focusing on big sound systems and safe spaces.
Joining him is Ar Ais Arís co-organiser Hannah Hession, a Galway born and based DJ who has been playing an energetic mix of bass, breaks, dembow, garage and all things in between since 2019.

data.name: Sally Cinnamon
data.body:
When a DJ has been at the helm of the party for 25 years, you know they’re doing something right. Sally Cinnamon exemplifies a golden age of the Irish party, which some may be too young to remember.
For over two decades, she has been a mainstay in Irish nightlife institutions and now she’ll be making her long-awaited debut at the Cambium this weekend.

data.name: Governess
data.body: Chicago born Governess has been an integral part of the Irish Club Scene for over 10 years. Her sets are energetic and fun with a touch of nostalgia. She respectfully plays Vinyl as well as CDJs and never sticks to one genre, which always makes for an unforgettable and enjoyable time on the dancefloor.

data.name: Aoife Nic Canna
data.body:
Aoife Nic Canna has been a central force in the Irish dance music scene
since its first moves in the early 1990's. A founding member of the
seminal Horny Organ Tribe, and dubbed the first lady of Irish house by
Hot Press, she had regular appearances at culture-defining nights/clubs
like Cork's Mór Disco, Dublin's Temple of Sound, and Manchester's
Hacienda.

data.name: Some Dance to Remember: Donal Dineen & Donal Scannell
Local Groove
data.body:
Local Groove Records is a DJ duo and independent record label founded by two lifelong friends from Waterford, Ireland, brought together by a shared passion for digging records and uncovering forgotten gems. What began as years spent collecting vinyl and DJing together evolved into a distinctive sound rooted in rare boogie, disco, and world groove records. Known for their deep crates and carefully curated selections, Local Groove Records deliver energetic, groove driven sets packed with records rarely found on streaming platforms.

In 2025, they launched Local Groove Records with their debut release: a white label collection of disco edits featuring reworked material from a range of local Irish artists, with the next release already in the pipeline.

data.name: DJ Chartini
data.body:
Waterford’s Chartini is a vinyl DJ with a passion for collecting records and sharing the gems she finds along the way. Blending funk, boogie, Afro-disco and global sounds, her sets are shaped by years of digging and a collection packed with character. Her
Cambium debut is much anticipated.

data.name: Donal Dineen’s Backstory with t-woc & Guests
DJ Repoman
data.body:
DJ Repoman is a vinyl-hound and woodworker who divides his time between exotic hardwoods and tropical rhythms. Always looking for that record he's never seen before, from a country he's never heard of, which he then showcases at his weekly event at Rockaway Beach NYC


“I Scour the Planet , so you don’t have to”

data.name: Dufi
data.body:
Dufi, founder of Nurture Records, is a dedicated digger of timeless gems. His sound, spanning the warmer ends of house, breaks, acid & electro has brought him to clubs & festivals across Ireland & Europe.

He is a unique producer, with stand-out releases on Small Moves, All City, LowMoneyMusicLove & his own label Nurture finding their way into record bags worldwide.

data.name: Æ MAK
data.body: Æ MAK is the boundary-pushing musical world of Irish artist Aoife McCann, where art-pop, experimental electronics and fearless performance collide. Blending soaring vocals, immersive visuals and raw emotion, she crafts captivating live shows that are equal parts theatrical and deeply personal. Constantly evolving, Æ MAK continues to blur the lines between folk, alternative pop and electronic music, creating bold, genre-defying performances that linger long after the final note.

data.name: Marcus O'Laoire Sunday Service
data.body: As day turns to night at All Together Now, Marcus O’Laoire brings Sunday Service to the Bandstand, a two-hour journey through a lifetime of record collecting. House is the common thread, but that’s about where the rules end. Expect French touch, New York classics, West Coast oddities, overlooked disco, Balearic detours and the kind of records that don’t get played often enough.

data.name: Ali Daly
data.body:
Ali Daly is a Limerick-based DJ, radio host and much to the detriment of her
savings - a record collector. Known for eclectic, vinyl-led sets spanning disco, house, techno and leftfield gems, she’s part of the Sunday Spinners crew, the collective behind some of the finest day parties on Ireland’s west coast. When she’s not behind the decks, you’ll occasionally find her behind the counter at Downbeat Records Limerick, taking full advantage of the staff perks of getting first dibs on the latest arrivals.

data.name: Some Dance to Forget: DD and Special Guests
Niwar Ismat Issa (Live)
data.body:
Nîwar Ismat Issa is a composer, music producer, and multi-instrumentalist from Iraqi
Kurdistan. Trained in music composition and the qanun, a traditional Middle Eastern
stringed instrument, he is also skilled in oud, saz, tenbur, and piano. His work blends
the rich musical heritage of his Kurdish roots with diverse global influences, creating a
distinctive sound that resonates across cultures.

With over 15 years of experience in the music industry, Nîwar has composed for film
and television soundtracks and collaborated with artists from around the world. His
career began as a music instructor and performer—both solo and in ensembles—and
he has since evolved into a sought-after music director and composer.

data.name: Mooncup
data.body: Spanning genres and styles, their aim is to showcase the joy of the mix and get your gun fingers in the air. Expect to hear everything from dancehall and soca to bouyon and baile, rubbing up against a range of other sounds along the way.

data.name: Ben Bix b2b Little O
data.body: Bringing together two distinct yet complementary forces of the Dublin music landscape, this pairing fuses infectious, dance floor-ready global rhythms with cutting-edge sonic architecture. Together, they bridge the gap between global underground club culture and innovative electronic production.

data.name: The Sweet Spot - Collective Takeover
data.body:
Established by Blkcnvs during the summer of 2022 and currently hosting a monthly party in Dublin’s Project Arts Centre. The Sweet Spot is somewhere special where open-minded dreamers get together, unwind, and reconnect through music and dance. A spot for you to let go of the stress of day-to-day life and most importantly SHAKE RUMP because you deserve to feel good in your skin.
Pull up & let loose, see you at The Sweet Spot!

data.name: Johnny Carroll
data.body: Playing sunshine music for sunshine people.

data.name: Frawl
data.body:
For nearly 3 decades Frawl has been collecting records and sharing them far and wide. One of a few DJs that can take the reins all night long and regularly plays 8 hrs plus. Frawls dj sets are similar to his productions, broad and diverse, heavily influenced by African music, the Caribbean, sounds from Detroit, Chicago & New York.
His band, East West Assembly have a forthcoming album on Detroits Sound
Signatue and he has just remixed the mighty Yankari which is out now on Love universal.

data.name: CAOIMHÍN
data.body: CAOIMHÍN is a producer, singer, and multi-instrumentalist re-imagining old Ireland in a new age. His psychedelic beat-driven music combines traditional dance tunes, an Gaeilge and native Irish folk songs with elements such as sampling, gated vocal loops and ambient synth soundscapes, paying homage to the long lineage of indigenous Gaelic music on which he was reared while simultaneously breaking new ground at its frontiers.

data.name: Lonesome George
data.body:
Lonesome George’s song-writing (in both English and Irish language) deals with love, life and revolution; mental health, the treatment of refugees and the environmental crisis. These ideas are brought to life through multi-layered riff-led grooves; 4 & 5 part harmonies, ethereal & ambient pieces; rip-roaring reels and other dance rhythms; and a selection of flavours from various genres interwoven to create a unique sound; changing from song to song, all while remaining rooted in the Irish tradition. 

LG is  Joe Campbell-McArdle (guitar, vocals), Myles McCormack (mandolin, vocals), Catriona Ní Ghribín (accordion, vocals), Fintan Mulholland (flute, whistles, vocals), Tommy Moynagh (bodhrán, percussion)

data.name: Annie Craic
data.body: Trad Folkin Rocks take over The Last City for a full day of rhythm, rebellion and seriously good craic. Kicking off with a communal bodhrán workshop, the takeover moves through a genre-bending line-up featuring CAOIMHÍN, Ispíní na hÉireann hosting the infamous Citizen Céilí, Lonesome George, The Wran, Huartan and more—before the festival debut of Trad Folkin Raps brings trad into collision with hip-hop, and Trad Folkin Raves carries the city deep into the night. Expect ancient sounds, new energy and the rulebook comprehensively torn up.

data.name: The Last City All Ireland Cypher with Lil Skag, Ahmed with Love, Sugaboo, Beddyminaj, GOMIE + Special Guests
data.body:
GET YOUR COUNTY COLOURS OUT! Ahmed, With Love. brings the best MCs from all parts of the Emerald Isle to The Last City to put on a GAA-themed rap clinic!

Wexford's Lil Skag, Dublin's Sugaboo, Cork's Beddyminaj and Galway's GOMiE are hear to represent their counties with pride as they swap hurls for hooks and leave it all on the pitch (if the pitch was All Together Now).

data.name: Jinx Lennon
data.body: Jinx Lennon sings about what he believes is happening in the real world as seen through the eyes of his border schizo punk fffolk music emanating from the Irish borderlands  .Subjected in his youth  to the split screen of Republic Ireland and Northern Ireland volatile goings on and the sort of doublethink politics no one would wish on any young head thus  Jinx ended up throwing it all into a blender along with his favorite sci fi books and mindfuckery of living in joyless  holy Eire.Now he sings it all  with the aim of not making life any more unbearable for the listener overwhelmed by modern existence  with the rawness and coherent  d.i.y. and anti hero realness that any true head out there requires .Jinx has toured with John Cooper Clarke played antifolk festivals in Denmark Street  with the likes of Fat White Family and supported the Fall and Christy Moore  .His songs ‘Newry Bird’ and ‘We don’t see anything ‘ have become anthems in the pubs and open mikes from The Lagan to the Lee along with the mighty ‘Forgive the Cnts’.

data.name: Ria Rua
data.body: • Ria Rua (“Red Queen” in Irish) is known for her explosive and emotional performances. Her lyrics are pointed and personal but the themes are universal: sex, power and freedom. Expect grungy and electronic rock anthems – a dynamic fusion of electronic pulses, grunge undertones, and alternative embellishments. Her tracks often feature mesmerizing vocals that exude attitude, layered over a blend of industrial textures and introspective melodies – music that sounds like an angry soundtrack to the looming collapse. Some songs are guitar driven. Some sound like a helicopter crashing into a petrol station. Some have two drummers. All of them are driven my a single minded vision and urgency.

data.name: Bicurious
data.body: Since forming in Dublin in 2016, Bicurious have been making their mark on the rock scene throughout Europe. Their two albums (re)constructed (2021) and Your Life is Over Now… (2024)  have brought the band a cult fan following and drawn the scene’s attention. Bicurious’ new album Your Life is Over Now, released on iconic UK indie label Big Scary Monsters, was crowdfunded by their fans, who helped them raise over €9,000 towards the record. Gathering over 9.6 million Spotify streams, and with support from the likes of Guitar World, Audiotree, Metal Hammer and Hot Press, the band have made fans all over the world with their unique blend of rock, math-rock, post-rock and unforgettable melodies.

data.name: THUMPER
data.body: THUMPER are a Dublin six-piece delivering a huge, psych-soaked wall of sound powered by two drummers, four guitarists and an unrelenting live energy. Blending towering distortion with infectious melodies and irresistible hooks, they've become one of Ireland's most exciting alternative bands. Following their acclaimed debut album Delusions of Grandeur and a Choice Prize Album of the Year nomination, THUMPER continue to push their expansive sound to new heights with electrifying performances and bold new music.

data.name: LOST at The Last City
data.body:
Enfour

Enfour is a Dublin based DJ and co-founder of LOST. Kickstarting the club night back in 2018.. Moving to Valencia in 2022, he became immersed in the house, tech and progressive communities. He made a name for ambition and versatility as a DJ and promoter, carefully curating parties at Killing Time, La Fabrica de Hielo, and his music and food event, House Special. He’s soundtracked parties at iconic venues like Spook, Club Oven and Room, played for house music giants the Basement. Now back in Ireland and forging new paths for LOST as a collective and brand, he’s busy to sharing the experience, knowledge, and of course, the records he’s gathered in recent years.

Support: Jordan Nocturne, Timmy Stewart, Thomas Melchior, Andreas Llatas, Denis Sulta, Francisco del Garda, Narciss, Viers, Pablo Bozzi, Brame & Hamo, Boots and Kats, Waze & Odyssey.

Neacy 

Neacy (fka Dploya) has been a constant in the Dublin circuit for over a decade. Whether he’s behind the decks or running the show, he’s built a reputation for championing diverse & underground sounds and spotlighting local talent. In his capacity as the lead booker for Wigwam in Dublin he has an eclectic taste that spans across genres including progressive house, classic rave and techno, UK garage and breakbeat. A club promoter at his core, he also frequently DJ's in the Dublin underground circuit, playing regularly for the likes of Injector Sound and in secret after hours parties throughout the city. His recent accolades include a 3 hour opening set for heavy hitters DJ Heartstring in Index as well as other prominent support slots for Upper90, Pegassi & more. 

Support: DJ Heartstring, Upper90, Pegassi, Narciss, Juicy Romance & more

data.name: The Last Chance Saloon with Western Girls x Fancy Dan
data.body: The frontier has reached The Last City. For one afternoon only, the streets become The Last Chance Saloon - a rhinestone-soaked honky-tonk where outlaw DJs, rogue cowboys, glittering desperados and frontier misfits gather for one final knees-up. Saddle up. There are no second chances.

data.name: The Reds
data.body:
Blending rich vocal harmonies with a unique instrumental lineup, The Reds create a sound that is deeply rooted in traditions of Bluegrass as well as some elements of early Jazz and Country
Based in Dublin, The Reds are a powerhouse ensemble bringing a fresh energy to the Irish music scene. Fronted by a trio of seasoned multi-instrumentalists who, in their individual careers, have worked alongside some of the most respected names in contemporary music, including The Frames, Keywest, Robert John Ardiff, David Kitt  and Bluegrass legend Ron Block.

data.name: Daddee
data.body:
Daddee is a synth heavy, rock'n'roll five-piece from Dublin. They are a culmination of musical instruments played together to bring satisfaction to the ears. Their soaring grooves and electric melodies bring on a state of euphoria in even the most subdued curmudgeons. If you don’t like being sad and enjoy having fun they are most certainly for you.
Their main influences are Lcd Soundsystem, Courtney Barnett, Viagra Boys, Queens of The Stone Age, Wet Leg and New Order.

data.name: Ciarzy
data.body: True&True founder and resident DJ Ciarzy makes his long-awaited return to All Together Now, rejoining the festival lineup for the first time since his 2022 debut. Following a hiatus from music and a successful 2025 comeback, he returns to The Last City older, wiser, and eager to etch his name even further into the Irish music scene. Expect a journey filled with groovy basslines, tech‑house rollers, and surprises throughout.

data.name: Winemoms
data.body: Living by the ethos that dance music is anything BUT serious business, Winemoms are known for turning dancefloors upside down with their raucous yet whimsical selections. Their club night WineMixer is an extension of this, championing local acts alongside residents in chaotic B2B matchups with a focus on fun!

data.name: Corcra
data.body: • Corcra is known for delivering euphoric, high-energy sets that spark hands-in-the-air moments and unforgettable dancefloor memories. With a signature style rooted in House, Prog, and Disco, Corcra blends uplifting piano riffs, booty-shaking basslines, and a healthy dose of disco flair to keep the vibe electric from start to finish. Corcra curates smile-inducing sets that create genuine connections, turning dancefloors into spaces where strangers become friends and every drop becomes a moment to remember. Whether in a club, at a festival, or an underground party, Corcra brings the kind of energy that lingers long after the lights come up.

data.name: Justyna Koss
data.body:
Hailing from Gdansk, Dublin based DJ, Justyna has carved out a distinctive presence within the city’s electronic music scene.
Through a series of residencies and performances across clubs and venues, she has built a reputation for well-crafted, dynamic sets and a versatile sound.
Her cross-genre flexibility — seamlessly moving from groovy electronica to high - energy techno - has led her to perform at Ireland’s major music festivals.

data.name: For Nina
data.body: For Nina are an emerging Irish alternative rock band blending soaring melodies, shimmering guitars and emotionally charged songwriting into a powerful, cinematic sound. Balancing moments of quiet vulnerability with explosive energy, the band have built a reputation for captivating live performances and heartfelt, hook-filled songs. With a growing catalogue of acclaimed releases, For Nina are quickly establishing themselves as one of Ireland's most exciting new acts.

data.name: Joshua Idehen
data.body: Joshua Idehen is a poet, vocalist and multidisciplinary artist whose powerful spoken word meets jazz, electronic music, soul and club culture. Renowned for his commanding stage presence and deeply human storytelling, he explores themes of identity, community and modern life with equal parts wit, vulnerability and intensity. Whether performing intimate poetry or soaring over dancefloor rhythms, Joshua Idehen delivers unforgettable performances that are both thought-provoking and emotionally charged.

data.name: Messages of Peace with Greta Thunberg, Sorcha Richardson, Róisín El Cherif, Leila Doolan, Brian Brannigan, Abu Abed, Dan Lambert, and Aoife Dunne
data.body: We are truly honoured to welcome an inspiring group to the Temporary Bandstand today at 12:30 PM with contributions from Greta Thunberg, Sorcha Richardson, Róisín El Cherif, Leila Doolan, Brian Brannigan, Abu Abed, Dan Lambert, and Aoife Dunne for this special event.

data.name: Mantle
data.body: Formed in 2024 by four lifelong friends from Co. Kildare, Mantle are one of Ireland's most exciting emerging indie rock bands. Blending soaring guitar work, emotionally charged songwriting and powerful live performances, they've quickly built a reputation on Dublin's underground circuit with standout shows at venues including Whelan's and The Workman's Club. Inspired by the likes of Radiohead, Wunderhorse, Pearl Jam and Jeff Buckley, Mantle craft expansive, melody-driven songs that balance raw intensity with quiet vulnerability. With a string of acclaimed singles and a growing following, they're a band firmly on the rise and one to catch before they break through.

data.name: A Man To Pet (DJ Set)
data.body:
For the past  20 years, A Man To Pet has been a glitter-soaked pillar of gay culture,  the vibe higher wherever he goes — from London’s most iconic venues to stages across Europe and Latin America.

In London, you can experience his glorious madness at his fiery monthly residencies at Bistrotheque, Dalston Superstore, Not Another Show, The Divine, and The Devil wears JPG. He also leads the exuberant monthly party Basic Boys, alongside dancers and go-go performers, taking London’s queer magic to Berlin and Paris.

data.name: Paradise Cabaret hosted by Jane Norman
data.body:
Journey into a comically absurd, skilfully slick and stupidly entertaining Cabaret.

It’s time to ditch the old Gods and embrace the cultural revolution of colour, carnival and chaos. Frivolous entertainment melts serious culture, we blur the lines, blur the vision and refocus on a fantastical, art soaked future.

A comedy of Special guest hosts and an ever changing line up of dreamy acts from circus, dance, music with the funest weirdos and queerdos around.

data.name: Ben Reel
data.body: With over 30 years of songwriting and performing, Ben Reel has become one of Ireland's most respected singer-songwriters. Blending rock, folk, blues, Americana and soul, his rich vocals and heartfelt storytelling have earned him a loyal following at home and abroad. Having shared stages with artists including Jools Holland, The Cranberries and Nanci Griffith, Ben brings warmth, authenticity and timeless songs to every performance, delivering a set that's both soulful and unforgettable.

data.name: Call Super
data.body: Call Super is one of electronic music’s true originals. The London-born artist has built a global reputation for fearless, genre-blurring DJ sets that effortlessly drift between hypnotic house, deep techno, ambient textures and leftfield oddities. Equal parts selector and storyteller, every performance is an unpredictable journey, balancing dancefloor energy with moments of pure musical exploration. With appearances at the world’s most respected clubs and festivals, expect a set that rewards open minds, curious ears and those ready to lose themselves in the unexpected.

data.name: Talks in the Tent: John Cooper Clarke
data.body: Sharp-witted, razor-tongued and unmistakably iconic, John Cooper Clarke is the original punk poet. Rising alongside the punk movement in the late '70s, his rapid-fire delivery, dark humour and brilliantly observed verses have earned him cult status across generations. From influencing everyone from Joy Division to Arctic Monkeys—who famously adapted his poem I Wanna Be Yours—to selling out theatres worldwide, Clarke remains one of Britain's most captivating live performers. Equal parts poet, comedian and cultural icon, expect an unforgettable masterclass in words that hit just as hard today as they did nearly five decades ago.

YABI is a French-Caribbean DJ now based in Dublin, bringing a sound shaped by her time in Montreal’s global music scene. Her sets focus on heavy percussion and rhythm, blending Bouyon, Konpa, and Dancehall with Global Bass and Afro Tech.

Since moving here two years ago, she’s been settling in nicely, playing at local spots like Fidelity, Row Wines, and Lucky’s, as well as joining lineups for Dublin Modular, Honeypot, and The Foxgluv Show on DDR.

data.name: Ricky Chong
data.body:
Ricky Chong is an Irish-born DJ and record collector with a deep passion for music's past and present. Known for seamlessly blending timeless records across genres, his sets are guided by instinct, emotion, and an unwavering commitment to musical discovery.

Ricky's record-digging mentality and refined technical ability combine to create memorable journeys on the dancefloor. Rooted in underground culture, his sound honours the past while always looking forward.

data.name: Simon Merriman
data.body: Simon Merriman is a resident DJ at The Big Romance, known for all-vinyl sets of house, disco and groove-led dance music. Since focusing on vinyl in 2023, he has played listening bars, clubs and festivals across Ireland, blending slick edits, deep cuts and feel-good selections into warm, groove-led sets. Driven by a love of digging and a focus on the dancefloor, his sets are all about good vibes from start to finish.

data.name: New Tropicalistas
data.body:
New Tropicalistas is a Dublin-based vinyl DJ duo celebrating the richness and diversity of Brazilian music. Blending samba, MPB, reggae, soul, disco, boogie and deep Brazilian grooves, their all-vinyl sets take audiences on a journey through timeless classics, rare discoveries and dancefloor favourites.
Since launching in 2024, they've built a loyal following through sold-out events and regular residencies at Fidelity and The Big Romance, establishing themselves as one of Dublin's leading selectors of Brazilian music on wax.
Expect warmth, rhythm, and an irresistible invitation to dance.

data.body: DJ Breff is a Dublin-based selector with a passion for digging for sounds from around the world. From jazz roots to underground funk, disco and beyond, his monthly sets in The Big Romance & Fidelity share those discoveries in the dance - expect everything from soul classics to the latest, leftfield grooves

data.name: Shrem's Madonnathon
data.body:
To kick off his fifth annual Madonnathon at The Big Romance, Shrem presents a festival-first edition of his passion project, which has become a one-of-a-kind fixture on Dublin's nightlife calendar, drawing a devoted crowd of Madonna fans year after year. 
Expect a two-hour odyssey through four decades of Madonna's unparalleled pop catalogue, featuring nods to her newly released Confessions II, a wealth of her biggest hit singles, dancefloor anthems, iconic remixes, and a few surprises thrown into the mix.

data.name: Talks in The Tent: David O'Doherty
data.body: David O'Doherty is one of Ireland's most beloved comedians, renowned for his brilliantly offbeat humour, razor-sharp observations, and songs performed on his trademark tiny keyboard. Winner of the prestigious Edinburgh Comedy Award, he's appeared on Live at the Apollo, Would I Lie to You?, QI, 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown, and Have I Got News For You. Equal parts whimsical and wonderfully absurd, David's unforgettable live shows have earned him a devoted following around the world.

data.name: Long Island Sound
data.body: Dublin-born duo Long Island Sound (Rob Roche and Tim Nolan) craft euphoric yet introspective electronic music, balancing emotional depth with club-ready energy via their own Signs of Space imprint.

data.name: Karl Guest
data.body:
Karl Guest is a Dublin-based electronic artist renowned for his versatility behind the decks, seamlessly moving across genres to keep dancefloors moving and listeners engaged.

Drawing strong inspiration from the foundational sounds of Chicago house and Detroit techno, Karl's sets eﬀortlessly weave through Balearic grooves, chuggy disco, Italo, acid house and electro, creating dynamic journeys that balance energy, groove and atmosphere.

data.name: SAZ
data.body: SAZ is a Dublin-based DJ known for groove-led house, rolling basslines, and sets layered with disco touches, acid influences, and funk-driven energy. Inspired by artists like Sally C, Saoirse, Krystal Klear, and Kolter, her sound is built around rhythm, warmth, and creating movement on the dancefloor.

data.name: OneCanChan
data.body:
OneCanChan is a Dublin DJ with Chinese roots, shaped as much by time spent working in record shops - surrounded by an ever-changing mix of sounds - as by long, sweaty nights on the dancefloor. That experience runs through everything they do, grounding their approach in a genuine love for club culture and a deep respect for the dancefloor as a shared space.
Moving across different shades of house, from prog and Chicago to tech and disco, alongside acid, breaks and global influences, their sets are fluid and emotionally tuned. Warm, organic percussion is a constant thread, tying together a sound that’s guided more by feeling than
genre.

data.name: Billy Scurry
data.body: Billy Scurry is one of the most respected and influential figures in Irish dance music culture. Emerging from Dublin’s underground scene in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Scurry became synonymous with the rise of authentic house and techno music in Ireland, helping shape a generation of club culture through his legendary residencies, eclectic musical taste and uncompromising approach behind the decks.

data.name: George Feely
data.body: Over the past number of years, George Feely has cemented himself as one of Ireland's most sought after party starters. With an upfront and energetic ethos, George's approach to music is that of a house purist, while also ensuring that everyone on the dancefloor is having a bloody good time.

His studio work has seen him remixing and producing acts like Bon Voyage, Kneecap, The Prodigy, Kelis, Zombie Nation, Saint Sister, Mr Oizo, Kelis, Talos, Really Good Time,Ria Rua and more.. He’s currently working on his first solo album with David Holmes & Andy Bell (Ride/Oasis)

data.name: Holly Lester
data.body: Originally hailing from rural Northern Ireland, Holly Lester has been busy carving her niche in the world of house and techno since emerging from England’s north-west dance scene at the start of the last decade. Raw analogue jams rub shoulders with dreamy trance tinged melodies and swirling breakbeats, constantly driven by the distinct percussive energy that has become her trademark. With a penchant for the sounds of yesteryear, expect to hear early French house slammers and forgotten Detroit classics interlaced with her unique approach to modern-day house music.

data.name: Shake & Flow with Meg Wrenn
data.body:
Meg is a yoga, meditation & mindfulness coach from Dublin. Her love lies in teaching meditation, yoga & intuitive flow with a passion for facilitating connections and encouraging individuals to step out of their comfort zones, fully embracing the present moment. Finding tremendous fulfilment in guiding others on a path towards awakening their divine feminine energy through mana movement and dance Meg sees this as a process of liberation, freedom, and beauty involves embracing both softness and the untamed aspects of our inner selves.

Join Meg as part of the Elevate Fit Fest programme for a "Shake & Flow" class, where you will be guided through a vibrant & uplifting morning flow class with shaking & movement to awaken the body & get set for the day

data.name: BoxHitt with Project You Fitness
data.body: Join the team at Project You Fitness for a morning session where you can expect a great class, with great people, great laughs & a lot of hard work. Project You Fitness is a Limerick based gym which welcomes attendees to take the weight off, as life is hard enough, so step into this class, smile and train to the best of your ability. Rest assured, this class is suitable for all levels, with no experience or equipment required. This is a boxing inspired HIIT class which will get your heart rate elevated for the day. Whether you’re a complete beginner or looking to test yourself, this full-body workout is suitable for all fitness levels and we welcome all individuals to join us to throw some jabs, learn some moves and to have a great start to the day.

data.name: Hula Hoop with Aisling Browne
data.body:
Aisling is an Arvigo® Therapy practitioner, holistic menstrual educator, yoga & embodied dance teacher and women's circle facilitator. Her offerings weave holistic menstrual education, womb wisdom, feminine empowerment, ceremony, ritual & healing. She works with women and girls both in person, in schools and online. Her Maya Abdominal Massage practice is based in Co. Clare.

Aisling is passionate about empowering women with cyclical knowledge & wisdom of the womb as well as inviting them to find their flow through embodied movement.

Returning to Elevate Fit Fest for her third year this September and her first class at ATN, Aisling will be sharing a hoop dance ‘playshop’ where she will guide you through exploratory play and dance with a hula hoop. Satisfy your inner child with this fun, joyful experience as you learn some tricks, sequences and find your unique flow. Guaranteed to bring laughter& joy and set you up for a laughter filled day.

data.name: Come Paint with Me
data.body:
Come Paint with Me is a playful and expressive 45-minute portrait painting workshop that invites participants to explore creativity, colour, collage, and self-expression without the pressure of creating a “perfect” portrait.

Participants will begin with a partially completed portrait provided by the artist. Their challenge is to transform and complete the image using paint, paper, collage, drawing, scribbles, textures, and mixed media materials. They are encouraged to experiment, follow their instincts, and let the artwork evolve in unexpected ways.

Workshop Format:

During the session, participants will:

  • Receive a partially painted portrait as their starting point
  • Explore colour, shape, pattern, and texture through mixed media techniques
  • Add layers using paint, paper, collage, drawing, and mark-making
  • Experiment with creative choices
  • Develop a unique finished portrait
  • No previous painting experience is required. The workshop is designed for all ages and abilities, with an emphasis on play, exploration, and having fun.

data.name: Neurographics Workshop
data.body:
Neurographics is how we change the world, starting at the tip of our markers. This innovative, neuroscience-based, art-therapeutic method is a way of regaining authority of your mind, body and life; systematically making positive changes to your well-being and the world around you.

The best part about it is that while it is deep creative work, it is also a meditative practice that energises and invites movement, letting us shed those layers and improve neuroplasticity.

Yana is an artivist, a sustainability consultant and a Neurographics specialist, looking to bring sustainable change through a fun and creative learning experience.

Neurographics method is about mimicking nature through a science based creative methodology. It is truly an amazing tool and a useful skill that promotes mindfulness, wellbeing and a healthy nervous system. It allows us to leave old habits and patterns behind and build new neuro connections to bring about sustainable change for ourselves and the planet.

The Neurographics workshop is designed to teach the basics of the method, whereby we take a negative thought/emotion/pattern, express it on paper and transform it into a positive insight through a meditative art practice. In the process, we work with neurolinguistics and micromotorics, following a specific algorithm that allows us to tap into subconsciousness and reprogram our neuron connections for a positive outcome, creating new neuron pathways and improving neuroplasticity.

data.body:
Orla Tooher is a qualified boogie bounce instructor for six years and is joining Elevate Fit Fest again this September to bring the incredible popular trampoline based classes to the festival. Joining the lineup at Lovers Rock this year we will offer a hybrid model where attendees can do 1 on 1 off so more attendees to get to experience the fun of bouncing.

Boogie Bounce is a fun, high-energy fitness class performed on individual mini trampolines, combining cardio exercise, strength training, balance work, and dance-inspired movements into a low-impact workout. Suitable for a wide range of fitness levels, including beginners and those looking for a gentler alternative to high-impact exercise, the class provides an effective full-body workout while being kinder to the joints than traditional aerobics or running. Participants can expect to improve cardiovascular fitness, burn calories, increase muscle tone, strengthen the core, enhance coordination and balance, and boost overall energy levels. The uplifting music and supportive group atmosphere also help reduce stress, improve mood, and make exercise enjoyable, leaving you feeling refreshed, motivated, and accomplished after every session.

data.name: Huartan
data.body: Emerging from the Gaeltacht quarter of West Belfast, Huartan is formed by three Irish traditional musicians – Catriona Ní Ghribín, Múlú, and producer Stiofán Ó Luachráin – alongside masked performers embodying the síogaí (fairy folk). As Hot Press write, Huartan are “one of the key voices in a realignment of modern Irish music and culture”: rooted in decolonial and anti-capitalist ideals, their otherworldly live shows channel a mythic pre-Christian Ireland. In 2026, the band will be touring their self-titled debut album, featuring Gaeilge songs injected with “urgent, pulsating electronica” (Hot Press) and described by Chordblossom as “one of the most visionary albums from 2025”.

data.name: Nan Fee
data.body:
If a bothy ballad and a vintage French vinyl record had a baby, and it was raised on a windswept Hebridean island, it might sound something like the music of Nan Fee. With a powerful vocal range, a rich heritage in Irish traditional music, and having lived for five years on the Hebridean Isle of Eigg, Nan’s songs weave stories rooted in a deep connection to place, arranged with the whimsical precision of a Wes Anderson score. This is folk music that feels both ancient and original. 

Nan has performed throughout Ireland, Scotland and England including Electric Picnic, Westival, Tedfest, Howlin’ Fling and Lyric Theatre Belfast. Currently living in Westport, her newest single ‘Howlin’ will be released later this year.
